title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第三十六: 尒朱榮
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第三十六: 尒朱榮 Volume 48 Biographies 36: Er Zhurong

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮 子文暢 文略 從子兆 從弟彥伯 彥伯子敞 彥伯弟仲遠 世隆 榮從父弟度律 榮從祖兄子天光

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong; sons Wenchang and Wenlue; nephew Zhao; cousins Yanbo, Yanbo's son Chang, Yanbo's brother Zhongyuan, and Shilong; Rong's paternal cousin Dulu; and Rong's grand-uncle's grandson Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong; his sons Wenchang and Wenlue; his nephew Zhao; his cousins Yanbo, Yanbo's son Chang, Yanbo's brother Zhongyuan, and Shilong; Rong's paternal cousin Dulu; and Rong's grand-uncle's grandson Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮，字天寶，北秀容人也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, style name Tianbao, was a man of Northern Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, whose style name was Tianbao, came from Northern Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 世為部落酋帥，其先居尒硃川，因為氏焉。

translations.literal: For generations they were tribal chieftains; their ancestors lived at Erzhu River and took that as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served for generations as tribal chieftains. Their forebears had settled on the Erzhu River and adopted it as their clan name.

sentences.zh: 高祖羽健，魏登國初為領人酋長，率契胡武士從平晉陽，定中山，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu Jian, at the beginning of Wei Emperor Daowu's Dengguo reign, served as Leader-Chief of the Lingren, led Qihu warriors in pacifying Jinyang and securing Zhongshan, and was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu Jian, in the early years of Emperor Daowu's Dengguo reign, was Leader-Chief of the Lingren. He led Qihu warriors in the campaigns that pacified Jinyang and secured Zhongshan, and was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以居秀容川，詔割方三百里封之，長為世業。

translations.literal: Because they dwelt at Xiurong River, an edict carved out three hundred square li and enfeoffed them with it, to be their hereditary estate forever.
translations.idiomatic: Because the family lived on the Xiurong River, the throne granted them a domain of three hundred square li, which became their hereditary holding for generations.

sentences.zh: 道武初，以南秀容川原沃衍，欲令居之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daowu's reign, because Southern Xiurong River's plains were fertile and broad, he wished to have them move there.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Daowu's reign, seeing that the plains around Southern Xiurong River were rich and open, he wanted the clan to relocate there.

sentences.zh: 羽健曰：「家世奉國，給侍左右，北秀容既在髂內，差近京師，豈以沃鹆脊，更遷遠地？

translations.literal: Yu Jian said: "Our family has served the state for generations, attending at the sovereign's side. Northern Xiurong is already within the capital region and relatively close to the court—how could we move to distant lands merely for richer soil?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian replied: "Our house has served the dynasty for generations, attending at the sovereign's side. Northern Xiurong already lies within the capital region and is comparatively near the court. How could we be uprooted to distant country simply for richer land?

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 所居處曾有狗舐地，因而穿之得甘泉，因名狗舐泉。

translations.literal: At their dwelling a dog once licked the ground; they dug there and found a sweet spring, which was therefore named Dog-Lick Spring.
translations.idiomatic: At their settlement a dog once licked the ground; when they dug there they found a sweet spring, and the place came to be called Dog-Lick Spring.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鬱德、祖代勤，繼為酋長。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Yude and grandfather Dai Qin succeeded one another as chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Yude and his grandfather Dai Qin each in turn held the chieftainship.

sentences.zh: 代勤，太武敬哀皇后舅也。

translations.literal: Dai Qin was the maternal uncle of Emperor Taiwu's Empress Jing'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Qin was a maternal uncle of Emperor Taiwu's Empress Jing'ai.

sentences.zh: 既以外親，兼數征伐有功，給復百年，除立義將軍。

translations.literal: Being an imperial relation by marriage, and having further rendered meritorious service on several campaigns, he was granted exemption from corvée for a hundred years and appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: As a kinsman by marriage and a man who had repeatedly distinguished himself in battle, he was granted a century of corvée exemption and appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 曾圍山而獵，部人射虎，誤中其髀。

translations.literal: Once while hunting on a mountain enclosure, a tribesman shot at a tiger and by mistake struck Dai Qin in the thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while hunting in the hills, a tribesman fired at a tiger and accidentally hit Dai Qin in the thigh.

sentences.zh: 代勤仍令拔箭，竟不推問，曰：「此既過誤，何忍加罪。

translations.literal: Dai Qin had the arrow pulled out and never pursued the matter, saying: "This was plainly an accident—how could I bear to punish him?
translations.idiomatic: Dai Qin had the arrow drawn out and never pressed an inquiry. "This was plainly an accident," he said. "How could I bear to punish the man?

sentences.zh: 」部內咸感其意。

translations.literal: " All within the tribe were moved by his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone in the tribe was moved by his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 位肆州刺史，封梁郡公，以老致仕，歲賜帛百疋以為常。

translations.literal: He rose to Governor of Sizhou, was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery, retired on account of age, and received a standing annual grant of a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Sizhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery. When he retired on account of age, the court made it his regular stipend to receive a hundred bolts of silk each year.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was given the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，追贈太師、司徒公、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父新興，太和中繼為酋長。

translations.literal: His father Xinxing, during the Taihe era, succeeded as chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinxing succeeded to the chieftainship during the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 曾行馬群，見一白蛇，頭有兩角，咒之，求畜牧蕃息。

translations.literal: Once while driving a herd of horses he saw a white serpent with two horns on its head; he uttered a prayer over it, asking that his livestock multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while driving his horses, he saw a white serpent with two horns on its head. He prayed over it, asking that his herds might flourish.

sentences.zh: 自是牛羊駝馬，日覺滋盛，色別為群，穀量之。

translations.literal: From then on cattle, sheep, camels, and horses daily grew more abundant; sorted by color into separate herds, they were counted by the grain-measure.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his cattle, sheep, camels, and horses grew ever more numerous. Sorted by color into separate herds, they were counted by the bushel.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有征討，輒獻私馬，兼備資糧，助裨軍用。

translations.literal: Whenever the court launched a campaign, he would present his private horses and also supply provisions to assist military needs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court went to war, he presented horses from his own herds and supplied provisions to bolster the army.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛，特聽冬朝京師，夏歸部落。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was specially permitted to attend court in the capital in winter and return to his tribe in summer.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, he received special permission to attend court in the capital each winter and return to his tribe each summer.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，諸公王朝貴，競以珍玩遺之，新興亦報以名馬。

translations.literal: Each time he came to court, princes, dukes, and great nobles vied to present him with rare treasures, and Xinxing repaid them with famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court, princes, dukes, and great nobles competed to send him rare treasures, and Xinxing repaid them with fine horses.

sentences.zh: 位散騎常侍、平北將軍、秀容第一領人酋長。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and First Leader-Chief of Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and First Leader-Chief of Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 新興每春秋二時，恆與妻子閱畜牧于川澤，射獵自娛。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn Xinxing would regularly take his wife and children to inspect the herds in the rivers and marshes and amuse himself with hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn Xinxing would take his wife and children to inspect the herds in the rivers and marshes and pass the time hunting.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，以年老，啟求傳爵于榮。

translations.literal: During Emperor Ming's reign, on account of his advanced age, he memorialized asking to pass his title to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Ming's reign, feeling his age, he petitioned to pass his title to Rong.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was given the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，贈太師、相國、西河郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and King of Xihe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and King of Xihe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 榮潔白，美容貌，幼而神機明決。

translations.literal: Rong was fair-skinned and handsome in appearance; even as a child he was quick and decisive in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was fair-skinned and handsome, and even as a boy showed a sharp and resolute mind.

sentences.zh: 及長，好射獵，每設圍誓眾，便為軍陣之法，號令嚴肅，眾莫敢犯。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved hunting; whenever he set up an encircled hunt and rallied the crowd, he would arrange them in battle formation. His commands were stern, and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he loved hunting. Whenever he organized a hunt and gathered his followers, he drilled them in battle formation. His orders were strict, and no one dared defy them.

sentences.zh: 秀容界有池三所，在高山上，清深不測，相傳曰祁連池，魏言天池也。

translations.literal: Within Xiurong territory there were three pools on high mountains, clear and deep beyond measure. Tradition called them Qilian Pools; in Wei speech they were called Heavenly Pools.
translations.idiomatic: Within Xiurong territory stood three pools on high mountains, clear and fathomlessly deep. Tradition called them the Qilian Pools; in the Wei tongue they were known as the Heavenly Pools.

sentences.zh: 父新興曾與榮游池上，忽聞簫鼓音，謂榮曰：「古老相傳，聞此聲，皆至公輔。

translations.literal: His father Xinxing once went with Rong to stroll by a pool when they suddenly heard the sound of flutes and drums. He said to Rong: "The ancients handed down the saying that whoever hears this sound will rise to the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinxing once walked with Rong beside one of the pools when they suddenly heard flute and drum music. He told Rong: "The old tradition says that whoever hears this sound will rise to the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: 吾年老暮，當為汝耳。

translations.literal: I am old and in my twilight years; it must be for you.
translations.idiomatic: I am old now and near my end; the omen must be meant for you.

sentences.zh: 」榮襲爵，後除直寢、遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: " Rong inherited the title and was later appointed Attendant of the Direct Quarters and General of Roaming Attack.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong succeeded to the title and was later appointed Attendant of the Direct Quarters and General of Roaming Attack.

sentences.zh: 正光中，四方兵起，遂散畜牧，招合義勇。

translations.literal: During the Zhengguang era, when warfare broke out on all sides, he dispersed his herds, gathered righteous volunteers, and recruited fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era, when rebellion flared on every side, he broke up his herds and rallied volunteers to arms.

sentences.zh: 以討賊功，進封博陵郡公，其梁郡前爵聽賜第二子。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing bandits he was advanced to Duke of Boling Commandery; his former title of Liang Commandery was permitted to pass to his second son.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in suppressing rebels he was promoted to Duke of Boling Commandery, while his former title of Liang Commandery was granted to his second son.

sentences.zh: 時榮率眾至肆州，刺史尉慶賓閉城不納。

translations.literal: At that time Rong led his forces to Sizhou, but Governor Wei Qingbin shut the city and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Rong led his troops to Sizhou, but Governor Wei Qingbin closed the city gates and refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 榮怒，攻拔之，乃署其從叔羽生為刺史，執慶賓還秀容。

translations.literal: Rong in anger stormed and took the city, then appointed his uncle Yusheng governor, seized Qingbin, and returned to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Rong stormed and captured the city. He installed his uncle Yusheng as governor, took Qingbin prisoner, and returned to Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 自是兵威漸盛，朝廷亦不能罪責。

translations.literal: From then on his military power gradually grew, and the court could not punish or blame him.
translations.idiomatic: From that point his military power steadily grew, and the court was in no position to hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮吞杜洛周，榮恐其南逼鄴城，表求東援相州，帝不許。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong swallowed up Du Luozhou's forces, Rong feared he would press south toward Ye City and memorialized requesting to march east to aid Xiang Province, but the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong absorbed Du Luozhou's forces, Rong feared a southern thrust against Ye City and petitioned to march east and relieve Xiang Province, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 榮以山東賊盛，慮其西逸，乃遣兵固守滏口以防之。

translations.literal: Rong, seeing the rebels strong in the eastern provinces, feared they might break westward and sent troops to hold Fukou firmly against them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the rebels strong in the east, Rong feared they might break westward and sent troops to hold Fukou against them.

sentences.zh: 於是北捍馬邑，東塞井陘。

translations.literal: Thus he defended Mayi in the north and blocked Jingxing Pass in the east.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore defended Mayi in the north and blocked Jingxing Pass in the east.

sentences.zh: 尋屬明帝崩，事出倉卒，榮乃與元天穆等密議，入匡朝廷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Ming died in sudden circumstances; Rong then secretly consulted with Yuan Tianmu and others about entering the capital to set the court right.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Ming died suddenly. Rong then secretly consulted with Yuan Tianmu and others about marching on the capital to restore order at court.

sentences.zh: 抗表云：「今海內草草，異口一言，皆云大行皇帝鴆毒致禍，舉潘嬪之女以誑百姓，奉未言之兒而臨四海。

translations.literal: He submitted a defiant memorial saying: "Now within the seas all is turmoil, and with one voice people say that the late emperor met disaster through poison, that Pan Consort's daughter has been put forward to deceive the people, and that an infant who cannot yet speak is set to rule all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a defiant memorial saying: "The realm is in uproar, and everywhere one hears the same story: that the late emperor was poisoned, that Pan Consort's daughter has been put forward to deceive the people, and that an infant who cannot yet speak has been set to rule the empire.

sentences.zh: 求以徐紇、鄭儼之徒，付之司敗。

translations.literal: I ask that Xu He, Zheng Yan, and their kind be handed over to the Office of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Xu He, Zheng Yan, and their accomplices be handed over to the Office of Punishment.

sentences.zh: 更召宗親，推其明德。

translations.literal: Summon the imperial clansmen again and raise up one of proven virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Summon the imperial clansmen again and set up a ruler of proven virtue.

sentences.zh: 」於是將赴京師。

translations.literal: " He then prepared to march on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He then prepared to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 靈太后甚懼，詔以李神軌為大都督，將于太行杜防。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was greatly afraid and issued an edict appointing Li Shengui Grand Commander to lead troops and block him at the Taihang passes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was terrified and ordered Li Shengui appointed Grand Commander to lead troops and block him at the Taihang passes.

sentences.zh: 榮抗表之始，遣從子天光、親信奚毅及倉頭王相入洛，與從弟世隆密議廢立。

translations.literal: At the outset of Rong's defiant memorial he sent his nephew Tianguang, his trusted follower Xi Yi, and the steward Wang Xiang into Luoyang to confer secretly with his cousin Shilong on deposing and enthroning.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Rong submitted his defiant memorial, he sent his nephew Tianguang, his trusted follower Xi Yi, and the steward Wang Xiang into Luoyang to confer secretly with his cousin Shilong on deposing the old ruler and enthroning a new one.

sentences.zh: 天光乃見莊帝，具論榮心，帝許之。

translations.literal: Tianguang then saw Emperor Zhuang and fully explained Rong's intentions; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang then met with the future Emperor Xiaozhuang and laid out Rong's plan in full; the prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 天光等還北，榮發晉陽，猶疑所立，乃以銅鑄孝文及咸陽王禧等五王子孫像，成者當奉為主。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others returned north, Rong set out from Jinyang. Still uncertain whom to enthrone, he cast bronze images of Emperor Xiaowen and the descendants of the five princes including Prince Xianyang of Xianyang, and whoever among them was successfully cast would be made sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang and the others returned north, Rong marched out from Jinyang. Still uncertain whom to enthrone, he cast bronze images of Emperor Xiaowen and of the descendants of the five princes, including Prince Xianyang of Xianyang. Whoever among them cast successfully would be made sovereign.

sentences.zh: 唯莊帝獨就。

translations.literal: Only the image of Emperor Zhuang came out whole.
translations.idiomatic: Only the image of the future Emperor Xiaozhuang came out whole.

sentences.zh: 師次河內，重遣王相密迎莊帝與帝兄彭城王邵、弟始平王子正。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Henei, he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to welcome Emperor Zhuang, the emperor's elder brother Prince Shao of Pengcheng, and his younger brother Prince Zizheng of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Henei, he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to bring out the future emperor, his elder brother Prince Shao of Pengcheng, and his younger brother Prince Zizheng of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 武泰元年四月，莊帝自高渚度，至榮軍，將士咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Wutai, Emperor Zhuang crossed from Gaozhu and reached Rong's army; officers and soldiers all shouted "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Wutai, the future emperor crossed from Gaozhu and reached Rong's camp. Officers and soldiers alike shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 及莊帝即位，詔以榮為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、開府、尚書令、領軍將軍、領左右、太原王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, an edict appointed Rong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Court, Grand General, Opener of an Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Guards, Director of the Left and Right, and King of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, an edict appointed Rong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Court, Grand General, Opener of an Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Guards, Director of the Left and Right, and King of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及度河，太后乃下發入道，內外百官皆向河橋迎駕。

translations.literal: When they crossed the river, the empress dowager had her head shaved and entered the religious life; officials inside and outside the court all went to Heqiao to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After they crossed the river, the empress dowager had her head shaved and entered religious life. Officials throughout the court went to Heqiao to welcome the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 榮惑武衛將軍費穆之言，謂天下乘機可取，乃譎朝士共為盟誓，將向河陰西北三里。

translations.literal: Rong was swayed by the words of General of Martial Guards Fei Mu, who said the realm could be seized at this moment. He deceived the court officials into making a joint oath of allegiance and led them toward a place three li northwest of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was swayed by General of Martial Guards Fei Mu, who told him the realm could be seized at this moment. He deceived the court officials into swearing a joint oath of allegiance and led them toward a place three li northwest of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 至南北長堤，悉命下馬西度，即遣胡騎四面圍之。

translations.literal: When they reached the north-south long embankment, he ordered them all to dismount and cross westward, then sent barbarian cavalry to surround them on every side.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the north-south embankment, he ordered them all to dismount and cross to the west, then sent his barbarian cavalry to surround them on every side.

sentences.zh: 妄言丞相高陽王欲反，殺百官王公卿士二千餘人，皆斂手就戮。

translations.literal: Falsely claiming that Chancellor Prince Gao of Gaoyang intended rebellion, he killed more than two thousand officials, princes, dukes, and ministers, all of whom submitted without resistance to slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Falsely claiming that Chancellor Prince Gao of Gaoyang intended rebellion, he slaughtered more than two thousand officials, princes, dukes, and ministers, every one of them submitting without a struggle.

sentences.zh: 又命二三十人拔刀走行宮。

translations.literal: He also ordered twenty or thirty men to draw swords and run toward the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered twenty or thirty men to draw their swords and rush the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 莊帝及彭城王、霸城王俱出帳。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang, Prince of Pengcheng, and Prince of Bacheng all came out of the tent together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang, the Prince of Pengcheng, and the Prince of Bacheng all came out of the tent together.

sentences.zh: 榮先遣并州人郭羅察共西部高車叱列殺鬼在帝左右，相與為應。

translations.literal: Rong had already sent the Bingzhou man Guo Luocha together with Chilieshagui of the western Gao-che to be at the emperor's side, acting in concert with the assailants.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had already placed the Bingzhou man Guo Luocha and Chilieshagui of the western Gao-che at the emperor's side to act in concert with the assailants.

sentences.zh: 及見事起，假言防衛，抱帝入帳，餘人即害彭城、霸城二王。

translations.literal: When the attack began, they pretended to be guarding him, seized the emperor and carried him into the tent, while the others immediately killed the two princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the attack began, they pretended to be protecting him, seized the emperor, and carried him into the tent, while the others immediately killed the Princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 乃令四五十人遷帝於河橋，沉靈太后及少主於河。

translations.literal: He then ordered forty or fifty men to move the emperor to Heqiao and drowned Empress Dowager Ling and the young sovereign in the river.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered forty or fifty men to move the emperor to Heqiao and drowned Empress Dowager Ling and the young sovereign in the river.

sentences.zh: 時又有朝士百餘人後至，仍於堤東被圍。

translations.literal: At that time more than a hundred court officials arrived later and were likewise surrounded east of the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred court officials who arrived later were likewise surrounded east of the embankment.

sentences.zh: 遂臨以白刃，唱云：「能為禪文者出，當原其命。

translations.literal: They were then confronted with naked blades, and a voice proclaimed: "Whoever can compose an abdication document may come forward and his life will be spared.
translations.idiomatic: They were then confronted with naked blades, and a voice cried out: "Whoever can compose an abdication document may come forward, and his life will be spared.

sentences.zh: 」時有隴西李神俊、頓丘李諧、太原溫子升並當世辭人，皆在圍中，恥是從命，俯伏不應。

translations.literal: " At the time Longxi's Li Shenjun, Dunqiu's Li Xie, and Taiyuan's Wen Zisheng—all celebrated writers of the age—were among those surrounded. Ashamed to obey, they prostrated themselves and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: " Longxi's Li Shenjun, Dunqiu's Li Xie, and Taiyuan's Wen Zisheng—all celebrated writers of the age—were among those surrounded. Too ashamed to obey, they prostrated themselves and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 有御史趙元則者，恐不免死，出作禪文。

translations.literal: There was an investigating censor named Zhao Yuanze who, fearing he could not escape death, came forward and composed the abdication document.
translations.idiomatic: An investigating censor named Zhao Yuanze, fearing he could not escape death, came forward and composed the abdication document.

sentences.zh: 榮令人誡軍士，言元氏既滅，尒硃氏興。

translations.literal: Rong had a man instruct the soldiers, saying: "The Yuan clan is destroyed; the Erzhu clan rises.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had a man instruct the soldiers: "The Yuan clan is destroyed; the Erzhu clan rises.

sentences.zh: 其眾咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " The troops all shouted "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: " The troops all shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 榮遂鑄金為己像，數四不成。

translations.literal: Rong then cast a golden image of himself, but after several attempts it would not come out right.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then tried to cast a golden image of himself, but after several attempts it would not come out right.

sentences.zh: 時榮所信幽州人劉靈助善卜占，言今時人事未可。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Lingzhu of Youzhou, whom Rong trusted and who was skilled in divination, said the present moment was not favorable for such an undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Lingzhu of Youzhou, a diviner whom Rong trusted, said the moment was not favorable for such an undertaking.

sentences.zh: 榮乃曰：「若我作不吉，當迎天穆立之。

translations.literal: Rong then said: "If it is inauspicious for me to take the throne, then Tianmu should be welcomed and enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then said: "If it is inauspicious for me to take the throne, then Tianmu should be brought in and enthroned.

sentences.zh: 」靈助曰：「天穆亦不吉，唯長樂王有王兆耳。

translations.literal: " Lingzhu said: "Tianmu is also inauspicious; only the Prince of Changle shows the signs of kingship.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingzhu said: "Tianmu is also inauspicious. Only the Prince of Changle shows the signs of kingship.

sentences.zh: 」榮亦精神恍惚，不自支持，遂便愧悔。

translations.literal: " Rong too was dazed in spirit and could not steady himself, and so was overcome with shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong too was dazed and could not steady himself, and was overcome with shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 至四更中，乃迎莊帝，望馬首叩頭請死。

translations.literal: By the fourth watch he welcomed Emperor Zhuang back, bowed his head to the horse's neck, and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth watch he welcomed Emperor Xiaozhuang back, bowed his head to the horse's neck, and begged to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 其士馬三千餘騎，既濫殺朝士，乃不敢入京，即欲向北為移都之計。

translations.literal: His three thousand-odd horsemen, having wantonly slaughtered court officials, dared not enter the capital and at once planned to move north and relocate the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His three thousand-odd horsemen, having wantonly slaughtered court officials, dared not enter the capital and at once planned to move north and relocate the court.

sentences.zh: 持疑經日，始奉駕向洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Hesitating for several days, he finally escorted the imperial carriage toward the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: After hesitating for several days, he finally escorted the imperial carriage toward the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 及上北芒，視城闕，復懷畏懼，不肯更前。

translations.literal: When they ascended Northern Mang and looked upon the city towers, he again felt fear and would not go farther.
translations.idiomatic: When they ascended Northern Mang and looked upon the city towers, he was seized by fear again and would go no farther.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍汎禮苦執不聽，復前入城，不朝戍。

translations.literal: General of Martial Guards Fan Li earnestly pressed him but could not prevail; he went forward into the city but did not attend court the next morning.
translations.idiomatic: General of Martial Guards Fan Li pressed him earnestly but could not prevail. Rong went forward into the city but did not attend court the next morning.

sentences.zh: 北來之人，皆乘馬入殿。

translations.literal: Those who had come from the north all rode horses into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had come from the north all rode their horses into the hall.

sentences.zh: 諸貴死散，無復次序。

translations.literal: The great nobles were dead or scattered, and court order was gone.
translations.idiomatic: The great nobles were dead or scattered, and court order had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 莊帝左右，唯有故舊數人。

translations.literal: At Emperor Zhuang's side there remained only a few old associates.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xiaozhuang's side there remained only a few old associates.

sentences.zh: 榮猶執移都之議，上亦無以拒焉。

translations.literal: Rong still clung to the plan to move the capital, and the emperor had no way to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Rong still clung to the plan to move the capital, and the emperor had no way to refuse.

sentences.zh: 又在明光殿重謝河橋之事，誓言無復二心。

translations.literal: He again apologized in Mingguang Hall for the affair at Heqiao and swore he would never again harbor divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingguang Hall he apologized again for the massacre at Heqiao and swore he would never again harbor divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 莊帝自起止之，因復為榮誓，言無疑心。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang himself rose to stop him and in turn swore an oath to Rong, saying he harbored no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang himself rose to stop him and in turn swore an oath to Rong, saying he harbored no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 榮喜，因求酒一遍。

translations.literal: Rong was pleased and asked for wine to be passed around once.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was pleased and asked for wine to be passed around.

sentences.zh: 及醉熟，帝欲誅之，左右苦諫乃止。

translations.literal: When he was thoroughly drunk, the emperor wished to execute him, but those at his side earnestly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When he was thoroughly drunk, the emperor wished to execute him, but those at his side earnestly remonstrated and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 即以床輦向中常侍省。

translations.literal: He was then carried on a couch-litter to the Directorate of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was then carried on a couch-litter to the Directorate of Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 榮夜半方寤，遂達旦不眠。

translations.literal: Rong did not wake until midnight and then remained awake until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Rong did not wake until midnight and then lay awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 自此不復禁中宿矣。

translations.literal: From then on he never again slept within the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he never again slept within the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 榮女先為明帝嬪，欲上立為後，帝疑未決。

translations.literal: Rong's daughter had earlier been a consort of Emperor Ming; he wished the emperor to install her as empress, but the emperor hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's daughter had earlier been a consort of Emperor Ming. Rong wanted the emperor to make her empress, but the emperor hesitated and had not decided.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎祖瑩曰：「昔文公在秦，懷嬴入侍。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zu Ying said: "In antiquity Duke Wen of Jin was in Qin, and Huai Ying entered to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zu Ying said: "In antiquity, when Duke Wen of Jin was in Qin, Huai Ying entered his service.

sentences.zh: 事有反經合義，陛下獨何疑焉？

translations.literal: There are matters that run counter to convention yet accord with righteousness—why should Your Majesty alone hesitate?
translations.idiomatic: There are times when what runs counter to convention still accords with righteousness. Why should Your Majesty alone hesitate?

sentences.zh: 」上遂從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 榮意甚悅。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 于時，人間猶或云榮欲遷都晉陽，或云欲肆兵大掠，迭相驚恐，人情駭震。

translations.literal: At that time people still sometimes said Rong wished to move the capital to Jinyang, or that he intended to unleash his troops in a great pillaging; alarm followed alarm, and public sentiment was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: At that time people still whispered that Rong meant to move the capital to Jinyang, or that he intended to unleash his troops in a great pillaging. Alarm followed alarm, and public sentiment was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 京邑士子，十不一存，率皆逃竄，無敢出者，直衛空虛，官守廢曠。

translations.literal: Of the scholar-officials in the capital, not one in ten remained; for the most part they had all fled and hidden away, and none dared go out. The palace guards stood empty, and official posts lay abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of the scholar-officials in the capital, scarcely one in ten remained. Most had fled and gone into hiding, and none dared show themselves. The palace guard posts stood empty, and government offices were left unattended.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，上書謝愆。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this, he submitted a memorial apologizing for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong heard of this, he submitted a memorial apologizing for what he had done.

sentences.zh: 無上王請追尊帝號；

translations.literal: For the Prince of Supreme, he requested posthumous imperial honors;
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince of Supreme, he asked that posthumous imperial honors be granted;

sentences.zh: 諸王、刺史，乞贈三司；

translations.literal: for princes and regional inspectors, he begged posthumous appointment to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: for princes and provincial inspectors, he requested posthumous appointment to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 其位班三品，請贈令僕；

translations.literal: for those whose rank stood in the third grade, he requested posthumous appointment as Ministers-in-Chief and Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: for those whose rank stood at the third grade or above, he requested posthumous appointment as Ministers-in-Chief and Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 五品之官，各贈方伯；

translations.literal: for officials of the fifth grade, each was to receive posthumous appointment as a regional governor;
translations.idiomatic: for officials of the fifth grade, he requested that each be granted a posthumous title equivalent to a regional governor;

sentences.zh: 六品已下及白身，贈以鎮郡。

translations.literal: for those of the sixth grade and below, and for commoners without office, he granted posthumous titles of commandery and district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: for those of the sixth grade and below, and for commoners without office, he requested posthumous titles as commandery and district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 諸死者無後，聽繼，即授封爵。

translations.literal: For the dead who had no heirs, adoption was permitted, and titles and fiefs were immediately granted.
translations.idiomatic: For the dead who left no heirs, he allowed successors to be appointed and immediately granted them titles and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 均其高下，節級別科，使恩洽存亡，有慰生死。

translations.literal: He balanced high and low, set grades by rank in separate categories, so that grace would reach both the living and the dead and bring comfort to life and death alike.
translations.idiomatic: He balanced high and low, assigning honors by rank in graduated categories, so that imperial grace would reach both the living and the dead and bring consolation to the bereaved.

sentences.zh: 詔從所表。

translations.literal: An edict approved what he had memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his petition.

sentences.zh: 又啟帝，遣使巡城勞問。

translations.literal: He also reported to the emperor and sent envoys to tour the city and offer comfort and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported to the emperor and sent envoys to tour the city, offering reassurance and inquiry to the people.

sentences.zh: 於是人情遂安，朝士逃亡者，亦稍來歸闕。

translations.literal: Thereupon public sentiment settled, and court officials who had fled also gradually returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon public sentiment calmed, and court officials who had fled also gradually returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 榮又奏請番直，朔望之日，引見三公、令、僕、尚書、九卿及司州牧、河南尹、洛陽河陰執事之官，參論國政，以為常式。

translations.literal: Rong further memorialized requesting rotating attendance duty: on the first and fifteenth of each month, he would summon the Three Excellencies, Ministers-in-Chief, Masters of Writing, the Nine Ministers, the Governor of Sizhou, the Intendant of Henan, and the officials in charge at Luoyang and Heyin to discuss state affairs, making this a regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Rong further petitioned to establish a rotating attendance duty. On the first and fifteenth of each month he would summon the Three Excellencies, Ministers-in-Chief, Masters of Writing, the Nine Ministers, the Governor of Sizhou, the Intendant of Henan, and the officials responsible at Luoyang and Heyin to discuss state affairs, making this a standing practice.

sentences.zh: 五月，榮還晉陽，乃令元天穆向京，為侍中、太尉公、錄尚書事、京畿大都督，兼領軍將軍，封上党王，樹置腹心在列職，舉止所為，皆由其意。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Rong returned to Jinyang and then ordered Yuan Tianmu to go to the capital, appointing him Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and concurrently General Who Leads the Army, enfeoffing him as Prince of Shangdang. He planted trusted intimates in every post, and their conduct and actions all followed his will.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Rong returned to Jinyang and sent Yuan Tianmu to the capital, appointing him Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and concurrently General Who Leads the Army, with the title Prince of Shangdang. He placed trusted intimates in every office, and their conduct and actions all followed his will.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔加榮柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an edict added to Rong the title Grand General Who Is the Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict promoted Rong to Grand General Who Is the Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮向京師，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong was advancing on the capital, and his forces were said to number a million.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ge Rong was marching on the capital, and his forces were said to number a million.

sentences.zh: 州刺史李神俊閉門自守。

translations.literal: The provincial inspector Li Shenjun closed his gates and held the city in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangzhou inspector Li Shenjun closed his gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 榮率精騎七千，馬皆有副，倍道兼行，東出滏口。

translations.literal: Rong led seven thousand elite horsemen, each horse having a spare mount, traveling by forced marches day and night, and marched east out through Fakou.
translations.idiomatic: Rong led seven thousand elite horsemen, each rider with a spare mount, and by forced marches day and night marched east through Fakou.

sentences.zh: 而與葛榮眾寡非敵。

translations.literal: Yet in numbers he was no match for Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his force was far too small to match Ge Rong's army.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞之，喜見於色，乃令其眾辦長繩，至便縛取。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong heard of this, his delight showed on his face, and he ordered his troops to prepare long ropes so that when Rong arrived they could bind and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong heard of this, his delight showed plainly on his face. He ordered his troops to prepare long ropes so that when Rong arrived they could bind and capture him alive.

sentences.zh: 自鄴以北，列陣數十里，箕張而進。

translations.literal: From Ye northward he drew up battle lines for several tens of li and advanced with wings spread like a winnowing basket.
translations.idiomatic: From Ye northward he drew up battle lines stretching for dozens of li and advanced with his wings spread wide.

sentences.zh: 榮潛軍山谷為奇兵，分督將已上三人為一處，處有數百騎，令所在揚塵鼓噪，使賊不測多少。

translations.literal: Rong hid troops in valleys and ravines as a surprise force, dividing commanders of colonel rank and above into groups of three at each point, each point having several hundred horsemen, and ordering them wherever they were to raise dust and make clamor so the enemy could not tell how many there were.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hid troops in valleys and ravines as a surprise force, grouping commanders of colonel rank and above in threes at each position, each with several hundred horsemen, and ordering them to raise dust and make a clamor wherever they appeared so the enemy could not tell how many they faced.

sentences.zh: 又以人馬逼戰，刀不如棒。

translations.literal: He also reasoned that in close combat between men and horses, blades were inferior to clubs.
translations.idiomatic: He also reasoned that in close combat between mounted men, blades were less effective than clubs.

sentences.zh: 密勒軍士，馬上各齎袖棒一枚，至戰時，慮廢騰逐，不聽斬級，使以棒，棒之而已。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered the soldiers that each man on horseback was to carry one sleeve-club, and that when battle came, fearing that pursuit would be wasted in chasing down kills, they were not to behead the enemy for counting heads but were simply to use the clubs—club them and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered every mounted soldier to carry a short club in his sleeve, and when battle came, fearing that the chase for severed heads would waste the momentum of pursuit, he forbade decapitation for tallying kills. They were simply to use the clubs and beat the enemy down.

sentences.zh: 乃分命壯勇，所當衝突。

translations.literal: He then assigned the brave and strong men each to the point where they would charge and break through.
translations.idiomatic: He then assigned the bravest and strongest men to the points where they would break through the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 號令嚴明，將士同奮。

translations.literal: His orders were strict and clear, and officers and soldiers fought together with one spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were strict and clear, and officers and soldiers fought as one.

sentences.zh: 身自陷陣，出於賊後，表裏合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He himself plunged into the battle line, emerging behind the enemy, and struck from within and without together, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He himself plunged into the battle line and emerged behind the enemy, and his forces struck from front and rear together, inflicting a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 于陣禽葛榮，餘眾悉降。

translations.literal: In the battle he captured Ge Rong, and the remaining troops all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle he captured Ge Rong, and all the remaining troops surrendered.

sentences.zh: 榮恐其疑懼，乃普令各從所樂，親屬相隨，任所居止。

translations.literal: Rong feared they would grow suspicious and afraid, so he broadly ordered that each man might go where he pleased, with kin following along, and settle wherever he chose.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the captives would grow suspicious and panic, Rong broadly ordered that each man might go where he pleased, with relatives free to follow, and settle wherever he chose.

sentences.zh: 於是群情喜悅，登即四散，數十萬眾，一朝散盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the multitude was delighted, and at once they scattered in all directions; several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the captives were delighted, and at once they scattered in all directions. Several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 待出百里之外，乃始分道押領，隨便安置，咸得其宜。

translations.literal: After they had gone a hundred li beyond, he then began to lead them away in separate groups and settle them wherever appropriate, and all found suitable placement.
translations.idiomatic: After they had gone a hundred li away, he then began to escort them in separate groups and settle them wherever appropriate, and all were placed suitably.

sentences.zh: 獲其渠帥，量才授用，新附者咸安。

translations.literal: Those rebel leaders who were captured he employed according to their abilities, and the newly submitted all felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders he captured he employed according to their abilities, and the newly submitted all felt secure.

sentences.zh: 時人服其處分機速。

translations.literal: People of the time admired the speed and decisiveness of his disposition.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired the speed and decisiveness with which he handled the matter.

sentences.zh: 乃檻車送葛榮赴闕。

translations.literal: He then sent Ge Rong to the palace in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Ge Rong to the capital in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 詔加榮大丞相、都督河北畿外諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict added to Rong the titles Grand Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Hebei and Beyond the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Rong to Grand Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Hebei and beyond the capital region.

sentences.zh: 初，榮將討葛榮，軍次襄垣，遂大獵，有雙兔起于馬前，榮彎弓誓之曰：「中則禽葛榮，不中則否。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, his army halted at Xiangyuan and then went on a great hunt. A pair of hares rose before his horse, and Rong bent his bow and swore: "If I hit them, I shall capture Ge Rong; if not, I shall not.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, his army halted at Xiangyuan and then went on a great hunt. A pair of hares sprang up before his horse, and Rong bent his bow and swore: "If I hit them, I shall capture Ge Rong; if not, I shall not.

sentences.zh: 」既而並應弦而殪，三軍咸悅。

translations.literal: " Both then fell at the release of the bowstring, and the whole army rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: " Both hares fell at the release of the bowstring, and the whole army rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 及後，命立碑於其所，號雙兔碑。

translations.literal: Later he ordered a stele erected at that place, called the Stele of the Two Hares.
translations.idiomatic: Later he ordered a stele erected at that spot, called the Stele of the Two Hares.

sentences.zh: 又將戰，夜夢一人從葛榮索千牛刀，葛榮初不肯與，此人自稱己是道武皇帝，葛榮乃奉刀，此人手持授榮。

translations.literal: Again, on the eve of battle, he dreamed that a man demanded a thousand-cattle blade from Ge Rong; Ge Rong at first refused to give it, but the man declared himself to be Emperor Daowu, whereupon Ge Rong presented the blade, and the man handed it to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Again, on the eve of battle, he dreamed that a man demanded a thousand-cattle blade from Ge Rong. Ge Rong at first refused, but the man declared himself to be Emperor Daowu, whereupon Ge Rong surrendered the blade, and the man handed it to Rong.

sentences.zh: 寤而喜。

translations.literal: When he woke he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he was delighted.

sentences.zh: 自知必勝。

translations.literal: He knew himself certain to win.
translations.idiomatic: He knew that he was certain to win.

sentences.zh: 又詔以冀州之長樂、相州之南趙、定州之博陵、滄州之浮陽、平州之遼西、燕州之上穀、幽州之漁陽七郡，各萬戶，通前滿十萬。

translations.literal: An edict further granted the seven commanderies of Changlo in Jizhou, Nanzhao in Xiangzhou, Boling in Dingzhou, Fuyang in Cangzhou, Liaoxi in Pingzhou, Shanggu in Yanzhou, and Yuyang in Youzhou, each with ten thousand households, bringing the total with previous grants to one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict further granted him the seven commanderies of Changlo in Jizhou, Nanzhao in Xiangzhou, Boling in Dingzhou, Fuyang in Cangzhou, Liaoxi in Pingzhou, Shanggu in Yanzhou, and Yuyang in Youzhou, each with ten thousand households, bringing his total fief to one hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 為太原國邑，又加位太師。

translations.literal: This became the domain of the State of Taiyuan, and he was further given the rank of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: This became the domain of the State of Taiyuan, and he was further promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 建義初，北海王元顥南奔梁，梁立為魏主，資以兵將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi reign, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, fled south to Liang, and Liang installed him as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi reign, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, fled south to Liang. Liang installed him as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and generals.

sentences.zh: 時邢杲以三齊應顥。

translations.literal: At that time Xing Gao rallied the Three Qi in support of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xing Gao rallied the Three Qi in support of Hao.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以顥孤弱，永安二年春，詔元天穆先平齊地，然後征顥。

translations.literal: The court considered Hao isolated and weak, and in the spring of the second year of Yong'an an edict ordered Yuan Tianmu first to pacify Qi territory and then campaign against Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The court considered Hao isolated and weak, and in the spring of the second year of Yong'an an edict ordered Yuan Tianmu first to pacify Qi territory and then march against Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥乘虛徑進，榮陽、武牢並不守，車駕出居河北。

translations.literal: Hao seized the opening and pressed straight forward; Rongyang and Wulao were both left undefended, and the imperial carriage went out to dwell north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Hao seized the opening and pressed straight forward. Rongyang and Wulao were both abandoned, and the imperial carriage withdrew north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，馳傳朝行宮於上党之長子，輿駕於是南趣。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this, he raced by post relay to attend the emperor at the traveling palace in Changzi in Shangdang, and the imperial carriage thereupon turned south.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong heard of this, he raced by post relay to attend the emperor at the traveling palace in Changzi in Shangdang, and the imperial carriage thereupon turned south.

sentences.zh: 榮為前驅，旬日之間，兵馬大集。

translations.literal: Rong served as vanguard, and within ten days troops and horses gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Rong served as vanguard, and within ten days troops and horses gathered in great force.

sentences.zh: 天穆克平邢杲，亦度河以會。

translations.literal: Tianmu conquered and pacified Xing Gao and also crossed the river to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu conquered and pacified Xing Gao and also crossed the river to join him.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸河內。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proceeded to Henei.

sentences.zh: 榮與顥相持於河上，無船不得即度。

translations.literal: Rong and Hao faced each other across the river, but without boats they could not cross at once.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Hao faced each other across the river, but without boats they could not cross immediately.

sentences.zh: 議欲還北，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: In council they wished to return north and plan a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: In council some argued for returning north and planning a later campaign.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎楊侃、高道穆等並固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others all firmly insisted that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others all firmly insisted that this would not do.

sentences.zh: 屬馬渚諸楊雲有小船數艘，求為鄉導。

translations.literal: Just then Yang Yun of the Mazhu clan had several small boats and offered to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yang Yun of Mazhu had several small boats and offered to serve as guide.

sentences.zh: 榮乃令都督尒硃兆等率精騎夜濟。

translations.literal: Rong then ordered the commander Erzhu Zhao and others to lead elite horsemen across by night.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then ordered the commander Erzhu Zhao and others to lead elite horsemen across the river by night.

sentences.zh: 顥奔。

translations.literal: Hao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hao fled.

sentences.zh: 車駕度河，入居華林園。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage crossed the river and entered and took up residence in Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed the river and took up residence in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 詔加榮天柱大將軍，增封通前二十萬戶，加前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: An edict added to Rong the title Grand General Who Is the Pillar of Heaven, increased his fief by a total of two hundred thousand households including previous grants, and granted him feather-canopied processional guards and martial music before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Rong to Grand General Who Is the Pillar of Heaven, increased his fief to a total of two hundred thousand households, and granted him feather-canopied processional guards and martial music before and behind.

sentences.zh: 榮尋還晉陽，遙制朝廷，親戚腹心，皆補要職，百僚朝廷動靜，莫不以申。

translations.literal: Rong soon returned to Jinyang and controlled the court from afar; kinsmen and trusted intimates were all appointed to key posts, and the movements of all officials at court had to be reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong soon returned to Jinyang and controlled the court from afar. Kinsmen and trusted intimates were all appointed to key posts, and every movement of officials at court had to be reported to him.

sentences.zh: 至於除授，皆須榮許，然後得用。

translations.literal: As for appointments and dismissals, all required Rong's approval before they could take effect.
translations.idiomatic: As for appointments and dismissals, all required Rong's approval before they could take effect.

sentences.zh: 莊帝雖受制權臣，而勤政事，朝夕省納，孜孜不已。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Xiaozhuang was constrained by a powerful minister, he diligently attended to government affairs, reviewing matters morning and evening without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Although Emperor Xiaozhuang was constrained by a powerful minister, he diligently attended to government affairs, reviewing matters morning and evening without cease.

sentences.zh: 數自理冤獄，親覽辭訟。

translations.literal: He repeatedly handled wrongful cases himself and personally examined petitions and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly handled cases of wrongful imprisonment himself and personally examined petitions and lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 又選司多濫，與吏部尚書李神俊議正綱紀。

translations.literal: Moreover, the selection offices were rife with abuse, and he discussed with the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Li Shenjun, how to restore proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the selection offices were rife with abuse, and he discussed with the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Li Shenjun, how to restore proper standards.

sentences.zh: 而榮乃大相嫌責。

translations.literal: But Rong greatly resented and reproached him for this.
translations.idiomatic: But Rong greatly resented this and reproached him for it.

sentences.zh: 曾關補定州曲陽縣令，神俊以階縣不奏，別更擬人。

translations.literal: Once, concerning an appointment to the magistracy of Quyang County in Dingzhou, Shenjun because of the county's low rank did not memorialize it and separately nominated someone else.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when an appointment to the magistracy of Quyang County in Dingzhou came up for approval, Shenjun, considering the county too low in rank to warrant a memorial, separately nominated someone else.

sentences.zh: 榮大怒，即遣其所補者往奪其任。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly angered and immediately sent the man he had appointed to seize the post.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was furious and immediately sent the man he had appointed to seize the post.

sentences.zh: 榮使入京，雖復微蔑，朝貴見之，莫不傾靡。

translations.literal: When Rong's emissaries entered the capital, though they were of low rank, the great officials at court, on seeing them, all bowed before them.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong's emissaries entered the capital, though they were men of low rank, every great official at court bowed before them.

sentences.zh: 及至闕下，未得通奏，恃榮威勢，至乃忿怒。

translations.literal: When they reached the palace gates and were not granted audience to memorialize, relying on Rong's power and prestige, they even grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the palace gates and were not granted audience to memorialize, they grew angry, relying on Rong's power and prestige.

sentences.zh: 神俊遂上表遜位。

translations.literal: Shenjun thereupon submitted a memorial resigning his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun thereupon submitted a memorial resigning his post.

sentences.zh: 榮欲用世隆攝選，上亦不違。

translations.literal: Rong wished to have Shilong act as interim head of selection, and the emperor did not oppose it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to have Shilong act as interim head of selection, and the emperor did not oppose it.

sentences.zh: 榮曾啟北人為河內諸州，欲為掎角勢，上不即從。

translations.literal: Rong had once memorialized that northerners be appointed to the provinces of the Henei region, wishing to form a pincer force, but the emperor did not immediately agree.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had once petitioned to appoint northerners to the provinces of the Henei region, wishing to form a pincer force, but the emperor did not immediately agree.

sentences.zh: 天穆入見論事，上猶未許。

translations.literal: When Tianmu entered audience to discuss the matter, the emperor still did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianmu entered audience to discuss the matter, the emperor still would not approve.

sentences.zh: 天穆曰：「天柱既有大功，為國宰相，若請普代天下官屬，恐陛下亦不得違。

translations.literal: Tianmu said: "The Pillar of Heaven has already rendered great service and serves as the state's chief minister. If he were to request replacing all officials throughout the realm, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu said: "The Pillar of Heaven has already rendered great service and serves as the state's chief minister. If he were to request replacing every official throughout the realm, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either.

sentences.zh: 如何啟數人為州，便停不用？

translations.literal: How can you memorialize for a few men to be made provincial governors and then halt and not use them?
translations.idiomatic: How can you petition for a few men to be made provincial governors and then refuse to appoint them?

sentences.zh: 」帝正色曰：「天柱若不為人臣，朕亦須代；

translations.literal: " The emperor said sternly: "If the Pillar of Heaven is no longer to be a subject, then I too must be replaced;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said sternly: "If the Pillar of Heaven is no longer to be a subject, then I too must be replaced;

sentences.zh: 如其猶存臣節，無代天下百官理。

translations.literal: but if he still preserves the conduct of a subject, there is no reason to replace all officials throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: but if he still preserves the conduct of a subject, there is no reason to replace every official throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」榮聞，大怒曰：「天子由誰得立？

translations.literal: " When Rong heard of this, he said in great anger: "By whom was the Son of Heaven able to ascend the throne?
translations.idiomatic: " When Rong heard of this, he said in great anger: "By whom was the Son of Heaven able to ascend the throne?

sentences.zh: 今乃不用我！

translations.literal: And now he will not use me!
translations.idiomatic: And now he will not heed me!

sentences.zh: 」語皇后復嫌內妃嬪甚有妒恨之事。

translations.literal: " When he spoke with the empress, he again complained of the inner consorts and of many matters of jealousy and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " When he spoke with the empress, he again complained of the inner consorts and of many matters of jealousy and resentment.

sentences.zh: 帝遣世隆語以大理，後曰：「天子由我家置立，今便如此。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Shilong to speak with her on principle of right conduct, but the empress said: "The Son of Heaven was installed by our house, and now he acts like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shilong to reason with her, but the empress said: "The Son of Heaven was installed by our house, and now he acts like this.

sentences.zh: 我父本日即自作，今亦復決？

translations.literal: My father could have made himself ruler on that very day—will he decide to do so again now?
translations.idiomatic: My father could have made himself ruler on that very day—will he decide to do so again now?

sentences.zh: 」世隆曰：「兄止自不為，若本自作，臣今亦得封王。

translations.literal: " Shilong said: "My elder brother simply chose not to do so himself; had he made himself ruler from the start, I too would now hold a princely title.
translations.idiomatic: " Shilong said: "My elder brother simply chose not to do so himself. Had he made himself ruler from the start, I too would now hold a princely title.

sentences.zh: 」帝既外迫強臣，內逼皇后，恆怏怏不以萬乘為貴。

translations.literal: " The emperor, pressed from without by a powerful minister and from within by the empress, was constantly discontent and did not regard the imperial throne as a blessing.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, pressed from without by a powerful minister and from within by the empress, was constantly discontent and did not regard the imperial throne as a blessing.

sentences.zh: 先是，葛榮枝党韓婁仍據幽、平二州，榮遣都督侯深討斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Lou, a remnant follower of Ge Rong, still held You and Ping provinces, and Rong sent the commander Hou Shen to campaign against and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Lou, a remnant follower of Ge Rong, still held You and Ping provinces, and Rong sent the commander Hou Shen to campaign against and execute him.

sentences.zh: 時万俟醜奴、蕭寶夤擁眾豳、涇，榮遣其從子天光為雍州刺史，令率都督賀拔岳、侯莫陳悅等入關討之。

translations.literal: At that time Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin held masses of troops in Bin and Jing, and Rong sent his nephew Tianguang as Inspector of Yongzhou, ordering him to lead the commanders Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and others into the passes to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin held large forces in Bin and Jing, and Rong sent his nephew Tianguang as Inspector of Yongzhou, ordering him to lead the commanders Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and others through the passes to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 天光至雍州，以眾少未進。

translations.literal: When Tianguang reached Yongzhou, because his force was too small he did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang reached Yongzhou, he did not advance because his force was too small.

sentences.zh: 榮大怒，遣其騎兵參軍劉貴馳驛詣軍，加天光杖罰。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly angered and sent his Cavalry Army Aide Liu Gui racing by post relay to the army to impose corporal punishment on Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was furious and sent his Cavalry Army Aide Liu Gui racing by post relay to the army to have Tianguang beaten.

sentences.zh: 天光等大懼，乃進討，連破之，禽醜奴、寶夤，並檻車送闕。

translations.literal: Tianguang and the others were greatly afraid and then advanced to campaign, defeating the enemy in succession, capturing Chounu and Baoyin, and sending them both to the palace in caged carts.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang and the others were terrified and then advanced to campaign, defeating the enemy in succession, capturing Chounu and Baoyin, and sending them both to the capital in caged carts.

sentences.zh: 天光又禽王慶雲、万俟道樂，關中悉平。

translations.literal: Tianguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daole, and all of Guanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daole, and all of Guanzhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是天下大難便盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great calamities of the realm were at an end.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the great calamities afflicting the realm were at an end.

sentences.zh: 莊帝恆不慮外寇，唯恐榮為逆。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang constantly gave no thought to foreign enemies and feared only that Rong would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang constantly gave no thought to foreign enemies and feared only that Rong would rebel.

sentences.zh: 常時諸方未定，欲使與之相持。

translations.literal: While the various regions were still unsettled, he had wished to keep them locked in mutual contention with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: While the various regions were still unsettled, he had wished to keep them locked in mutual contention with Rong.

sentences.zh: 及告捷之日，乃不甚喜，謂尚書令、臨淮王彧曰：「即今天下，便是無賊？

translations.literal: On the day victory was reported, he was not greatly pleased and said to the Minister-in-Chief, the Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu: "So now throughout the realm there are no more rebels?
translations.idiomatic: On the day victory was reported, he was not greatly pleased and said to the Minister-in-Chief, the Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu: "So now throughout the realm there are no more rebels?

sentences.zh: 」臨淮見帝色不悅，曰：「臣恐賊平以後，方勞聖慮。

translations.literal: " When Linhuai saw that the emperor's expression was displeased, he said: "Your servant fears that after the rebels are pacified, Your Majesty's concerns will only then begin to weigh upon you.
translations.idiomatic: " When Linhuai saw that the emperor looked displeased, he said: "Your servant fears that after the rebels are pacified, Your Majesty's concerns will only then truly begin.

sentences.zh: 」帝畏餘人怪，還以他語解之，曰：「其實撫甯荒余，彌成不易。」

translations.literal: " The emperor, fearing that others would find it strange, changed to other words to explain himself, saying: "In truth, to pacify and settle the remnant wilderness will be all the more difficult to achieve."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, fearing that others would find it strange, changed the subject and said: "In truth, to pacify and settle the devastated regions will be all the more difficult."

sentences.zh: 榮好射獵，不舍寒暑，法禁嚴重。

translations.literal: Rong loved hunting and archery and did not cease in cold or heat; the regulations and prohibitions were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Rong loved hunting and archery and did not cease in cold or heat, and the regulations he enforced were severe.

sentences.zh: 若一鹿出，乃有數人殞命。

translations.literal: If a single deer appeared, several men might lose their lives.
translations.idiomatic: If a single deer appeared, several men might lose their lives.

sentences.zh: 曾有一人，見猛獸便走，謂曰：「欲求活邪！

translations.literal: Once there was a man who, on seeing a fierce beast, ran away, and Rong said to him: "Do you wish to live?
translations.idiomatic: Once there was a man who, on seeing a fierce beast, ran away, and Rong said to him: "Do you wish to live?

sentences.zh: 」遂即斬之。

translations.literal: " He then immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then immediately beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 自此獵如登戰場。

translations.literal: From then on, hunting was like entering a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, the hunt was waged like a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 曾見一猛獸在窮穀中，乃令餘人重衣空手搏之，不令復損。

translations.literal: Once he saw a fierce beast in a deep ravine and ordered the others to wear heavy clothing and wrestle it bare-handed, not permitting any further damage to the animal.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he spotted a fierce beast in a deep ravine, he ordered the others to don heavy clothing and wrestle it bare-handed, forbidding any further harm to the animal with weapons.

sentences.zh: 於是數人被殺，遂禽得之。

translations.literal: Thereupon several men were killed, and thus the beast was captured and obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Several men were killed in the struggle, but the beast was finally captured.

sentences.zh: 持此而樂焉。

translations.literal: He took delight in this.
translations.idiomatic: He took delight in such sport.

sentences.zh: 列圍而進，雖阻險不得回避，其下甚苦之。

translations.literal: They formed encirclements and advanced; even when facing obstacles and danger they were not permitted to evade, and his subordinates greatly suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: They formed a beat and drove forward; even where the terrain was treacherous they were forbidden to hang back, and his followers found it unbearable.

sentences.zh: 太宰元天穆從容言榮勳業，宜調政養人。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu calmly said that Rong's meritorious achievements called for adjusting governance and nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu calmly suggested that, given Rong's meritorious service, it was time to adjust governance and nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 榮便攘肘謂天穆曰：「太后女主，不能自正，推奉天子者，此是人臣常節。

translations.literal: Rong then waved him off and said to Tianmu: "The empress dowager is a female ruler and cannot set herself right; to support and raise up the Son of Heaven—this is the ordinary obligation of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then brushed him aside and said to Tianmu: "The empress dowager is a woman holding power and cannot set things right herself; to support and raise up the Son of Heaven is the ordinary duty of a minister.

sentences.zh: 葛容之徒，本是奴才，乘時作亂，譬如奴走，禽獲便休。

translations.literal: Those like Ge Rong were originally bondsmen; they seized the moment to rebel—like a runaway slave, once captured it is finished.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ge Rong were bondsmen to begin with; they seized the moment to rebel. Like a runaway slave, once captured the matter is over.

sentences.zh: 頃來受國大寵，未能混一海內，何宜今日便言勳也？

translations.literal: Recently receiving the state's great favor, we have not yet unified all within the seas—how is it fitting today to speak of merit?
translations.idiomatic: We have only lately received the state's greatest favor, and we have not yet unified the realm—how can we speak of merit today?

sentences.zh: 如聞朝士猶自寬縱，今秋欲共兄戒勒士馬，校獵嵩原，令貪汙朝貴，入圍搏虎。

translations.literal: I hear that court officials are still indulgent and lax; this autumn I wish to join my elder brother in drilling soldiers and horses, conducting a hunt on the Song Plain, and making the corrupt court nobles enter the encirclement to wrestle tigers.
translations.idiomatic: I hear court officials are still indulgent and lax. This autumn I wish to join my elder brother in drilling troops and horses and hunting on the Song Plain, forcing the corrupt court nobles into the beat to wrestle tigers.

sentences.zh: 仍出魯陽，曆三荊，悉擁生蠻，北填六鎮。

translations.literal: Then go out to Ruyang, pass through the Three Jings, entirely drive the raw barbarians, and fill the Six Garrisons in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Then march out through Ruyang, pass through the Three Jings, drive all the unsubdued barbarians before us, and reinforce the Six Garrisons in the north.

sentences.zh: 回軍之際，因平汾胡。

translations.literal: On the return march, pacify the Fen Hu along the way.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, we will pacify the Fen Hu as we go.

sentences.zh: 明年簡練精騎，分出江、淮，蕭衍若降，乞萬戶侯；

translations.literal: Next year drill elite cavalry and dispatch them separately toward the Yangtze and Huai; if Xiao Yan submits, I request a marquisate of ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Next year we will drill elite cavalry and send columns toward the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan submits, I ask for a marquisate of ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 如其不降，徑度數千騎，便往縛取。

translations.literal: If he does not submit, with several thousand cavalry crossing directly, go and bind and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: if he does not submit, a few thousand cavalry will cross at once and go bind and capture him.

sentences.zh: 待六合寧一，八表無塵，然後共兄奉天子巡四方，觀風俗，布政教，如此乃可稱勳耳。

translations.literal: Wait until the six directions are at peace and unified and the eight regions are without turmoil; then together with my elder brother escort the Son of Heaven on tour through the four quarters, observe customs, and disseminate government and teaching—only thus can merit truly be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: When the six directions are at peace, the realm is unified, and the eight quarters are free of turmoil, then together with my elder brother we will escort the Son of Heaven on tour through the land, observe local customs, and spread government and teaching—only then may we speak of merit.

sentences.zh: 今若止獵，兵士懈怠，安可復用也？」

translations.literal: If we stop hunting now, the soldiers will grow lax—how could they be used again?"
translations.idiomatic: If we stop hunting now, the soldiers will grow slack—how could they ever be used again?"

sentences.zh: 及見四方無事，乃遣人奏曰：「參軍許周勸臣取九錫，臣惡其此言，已發遣令去。

translations.literal: When he saw that the four quarters were without trouble, he sent someone to memorialize: "Army Aide Xu Zhou urged me to accept the Nine Distinctions; I detest such words and have already dismissed him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw that the four quarters were at peace, he sent a memorial saying: "Army Aide Xu Zhou urged me to accept the Nine Distinctions. I detest such talk and have already dismissed him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 」榮時望得殊禮，故以意諷朝廷。

translations.literal: " Rong at the time hoped to receive extraordinary honors and thus used this to obliquely admonish the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong at the time hoped to receive extraordinary honors and used the memorial to obliquely prod the court.

sentences.zh: 帝實不欲與之，因稱其忠。

translations.literal: The emperor in truth did not wish to grant them and therefore praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang in truth did not wish to grant them and therefore praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 榮見帝年長明悟，為眾所歸，欲移自近，皆使由己。

translations.literal: Rong saw that the emperor was grown, clear-minded, and the object of popular allegiance; he wished to move the capital nearer to himself and have everything go through him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong saw that Emperor Xiaozhuang was grown, clear-minded, and winning the allegiance of the people; he wished to move the capital nearer to himself and have everything pass through his hands.

sentences.zh: 每因醉雲，入將天子，拜謁金陵後，還復恆朔。

translations.literal: Each time, after growing drunk, he would take the Son of Heaven in with him; after paying obeisance at the imperial precinct, they would return as before on the first of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Each time, after he had drunk himself into a stupor, he would take the Son of Heaven in with him; after paying obeisance in the imperial precinct, they would return as before on the first of the month.

sentences.zh: 而侍中硃元龍輒從尚書索太和中遷京故事，於是復有移都消息。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhu Yuanlong repeatedly requested from the Masters of Writing the precedents for moving the capital during the Tahe era, whereupon rumors of moving the capital arose again.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhu Yuanlong repeatedly asked the Masters of Writing for the precedents on moving the capital during the Tahe era, and rumors of a capital transfer arose once again.

sentences.zh: 榮乃暫來向京，言看皇后娩難。

translations.literal: Rong then came temporarily toward the capital, saying he wished to attend the empress's difficult childbirth.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then came temporarily toward the capital, saying he wished to attend the empress during her difficult childbirth.

sentences.zh: 帝懲河陰之事，終恐難保，乃與城陽王徽、侍中楊侃、李彧、尚書右僕射元羅謀，皆勸帝刺殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of the He'yin affair, ultimately feared he could not preserve himself; he then plotted with the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Li Yu, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo—all urged the emperor to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang, mindful of the He'yin massacre, ultimately feared he could not preserve himself. He plotted with the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Li Yu, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo, and all urged him to assassinate Rong.

sentences.zh: 唯膠東侯李侃晞、濟陰王暉業言榮若來，必有備，恐不可圖。

translations.literal: Only the Marquis of Jiaodong, Li Kanxi, and the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, said that if Rong came, he would certainly be prepared, and they feared it could not be attempted.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Marquis of Jiaodong, Li Kanxi, and the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, argued that if Rong came he would certainly be on his guard, and they feared the plot could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺其黨與，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: They also wished to kill his faction and raise troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: They also considered killing his followers and raising troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 帝疑未定，而京師人懷憂懼，中書侍郎邢子才之徒，已避之東出。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and had not decided, but the people of the capital were fearful; the Secretariat Gentleman Xing Zicai and others had already fled eastward to avoid trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang hesitated and could not decide, but the people of the capital were gripped by fear; the Secretariat Gentleman Xing Zicai and others had already fled east to escape the coming crisis.

sentences.zh: 榮乃遍與朝士書，相任留。

translations.literal: Rong then wrote letters to all court officials, mutually assuring one another to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then wrote to court officials throughout the capital, urging one another to stay and keep faith.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人溫子升以書呈帝，帝恆望其不來，及見書，以榮必來，色甚不悅。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Wen Zisheng presented the letter to the emperor; the emperor had constantly hoped he would not come, but on seeing the letter, knowing Rong would certainly come, his expression was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Wen Zisheng presented the letter to Emperor Xiaozhuang, who had constantly hoped Rong would not come. When he saw the letter and knew Rong would certainly come, his face darkened.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍奚毅，建義初往來通命，帝每期之甚重，然以為榮通親，不敢與之言情。

translations.literal: General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, who at the beginning of the Jianyi era had gone back and forth bearing communications—the emperor always placed great hope in him, yet because he thought Yi was close to Rong, he did not dare confide in him.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi had gone back and forth bearing communications at the beginning of the Jianyi era, and Emperor Xiaozhuang always placed great hope in him. Yet because he believed Yi was close to Rong, he did not dare confide the plan.

sentences.zh: 毅曰：「若必有變，臣甯死陛下難，不能事契胡。

translations.literal: Yi said: "If there must indeed be a crisis, your servant would rather die in Your Majesty's distress than serve the Jie barbarians.
