translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "If crisis must come, your servant would rather die in Your Majesty's cause than serve the Jie barbarians.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕保天柱無異心，亦不忘卿忠款。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "We guarantee that the Pillar of Heaven has no rebellious intent, and We shall not forget your loyal devotion."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "We guarantee that the Pillar of Heaven harbors no disloyal intent, and We shall not forget your loyal devotion."

sentences.zh: 三年八月，榮將四五千騎，發并州向京。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, Rong led four or five thousand cavalry and set out from Bingzhou toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, Rong led four or five thousand cavalry from Bingzhou toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 時人皆言其反，復道天子必應圖之。

translations.literal: People at the time all said he was rebelling, and again said the Son of Heaven would certainly attempt to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time all said he was rebelling, and again declared that the Son of Heaven would surely move to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 九月初，榮至京。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the ninth month, Rong reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the ninth month, Rong reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 有人告雲，帝欲圖之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that the emperor intended to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Emperor Xiaozhuang intended to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 榮即具奏。

translations.literal: Rong immediately memorialized in full.
translations.idiomatic: Rong immediately submitted a full memorial about it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「外人亦言王欲害我，豈可信之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Outsiders also say the prince wishes to harm me—how can such things be believed?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "Outsiders also say the prince wishes to harm me—how can such talk be believed?

sentences.zh: 」於是榮不自疑，每入謁帝，從人不過數十，皆不持兵仗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Rong did not suspect himself; each time he entered audience with the emperor, his attendants numbered no more than several dozen, and none carried weapons.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Rong put aside his suspicions. Each time he entered audience with the emperor, he brought no more than several dozen followers, and none carried weapons.

sentences.zh: 帝欲止，城陽王曰：「縱不反，亦何可耐？

translations.literal: The emperor wished to stop the plan, but the Prince of Chengyang said: "Even if he does not rebel, how can he be endured?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang wished to abandon the plan, but the Prince of Chengyang said: "Even if he does not rebel, how can he be endured?

sentences.zh: 況何可保耶？

translations.literal: And how can he be trusted to stay loyal?
translations.idiomatic: And how can his loyalty be trusted?

sentences.zh: 」又北人語訛，語「尒硃」為「人主」。

translations.literal: " Also, northern speech is imprecise: they pronounce "Erzhu" as "ruler of men."
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, northern speech slurs words: they pronounce "Erzhu" as "ruler of men."

sentences.zh: 上又聞其在北言，我姓人主。

translations.literal: The emperor also heard that in the north he said, "My surname is Ruler of Men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also heard that in the north Rong had said, "My surname is Ruler of Men."

sentences.zh: 先是，長星出中台，掃大角，恆州人高榮祖頗明天文，榮問之曰：「是何祥也？

translations.literal: Earlier, a baleful star appeared at the Central Terrace and swept through Great Horn; Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou, who was well versed in astronomy—Rong asked him: "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a baleful star had appeared at the Central Terrace and swept through Great Horn. Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou, who was well versed in astronomy—Rong asked him: "What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「除舊佈新象也。

translations.literal: " He answered: "It is the sign of removing the old and establishing the new.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "It is the sign of removing the old and establishing the new.

sentences.zh: 昔長星掃大角，秦以之亡。

translations.literal: In former times, when a baleful star swept through Great Horn, Qin perished because of it.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when a baleful star swept through Great Horn, Qin perished because of it.

sentences.zh: 」榮聞之悅。

translations.literal: " Rong heard this and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong heard this and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 又榮下行台郎中李顯和曾曰：「天柱至，那無九錫，安須王自索也？

translations.literal: Also, Li Xianhe, a bureau aide under Rong's mobile headquarters, once said: "When the Pillar of Heaven arrives, how could there be no Nine Distinctions—why must the prince ask for them himself?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianhe, a bureau aide under Rong's mobile headquarters, also once said: "When the Pillar of Heaven arrives, how could there be no Nine Distinctions—why must the prince ask for them himself?

sentences.zh: 亦是天子不見機！

translations.literal: It is also that the Son of Heaven does not read the signs!
translations.idiomatic: It is the Son of Heaven who fails to read the signs!

sentences.zh: 」都督郭羅察曰：「今年真可作禪文，何但九錫。

translations.literal: " Commander Guo Luocha said: "This year one could truly compose an abdication document—why stop at the Nine Distinctions?
translations.idiomatic: " Commander Guo Luocha said: "This year one could truly compose an abdication document—why stop at the Nine Distinctions?

sentences.zh: 」參軍褚光曰：「人言并州城上有紫氣，何慮天柱不應。

translations.literal: " Army Aide Chu Guang said: "People say purple vapor rises above Bingzhou city—why worry that the Pillar of Heaven will not receive his due?
translations.idiomatic: " Army Aide Chu Guang said: "People say purple vapor rises above Bingzhou city—why worry that the Pillar of Heaven will not receive his due?

sentences.zh: 」榮下人皆陵侮帝左右，無所忌憚，其事皆上聞。

translations.literal: " All of Rong's subordinates insulted and browbeat the emperor's attendants without any fear, and everything reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: " All of Rong's subordinates insulted and browbeat the emperor's attendants without restraint, and word of everything reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 奚毅又見，求聞。

translations.literal: Xi Yi again had an audience, requesting to report.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yi had another audience and asked to speak privately.

sentences.zh: 帝即下明光殿與語。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately descended to the Hall of Bright Light to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang immediately went down to the Hall of Bright Light to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 帝又疑其為榮，不告以情。

translations.literal: The emperor again suspected he was Rong's agent and did not confide the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang again suspected he was Rong's agent and did not confide the plan.

sentences.zh: 及知毅赤誠，乃召城陽王徽及楊侃、李彧，告以毅語。

translations.literal: When he learned of Yi's pure loyalty, he then summoned the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Yang Kan, and Li Yu, and told them what Yi had said.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of Yi's pure loyalty, he summoned the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Yang Kan, and Li Yu and told them what Yi had said.

sentences.zh: 榮小女嫁與帝兄子陳留王，小字伽邪。

translations.literal: Rong's younger daughter was married to the Chenliu Prince, the son of the emperor's elder brother, whose childhood name was Jiaye.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger daughter was married to the Chenliu Prince, son of the emperor's elder brother, whose childhood name was Jiaye.

sentences.zh: 榮嘗指之曰：「我終當得此女婿力。

translations.literal: Rong once pointed to him and said: "I will ultimately obtain this son-in-law's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Rong once pointed to him and said: "I will ultimately have this son-in-law's strength behind me.

sentences.zh: 」徽又云：「榮慮陛下終為此患，脫有東宮，必貪立孩幼。

translations.literal: " Hui further reported: "Rong worries that Your Majesty will ultimately become this threat; if there is an heir apparent, he will greedily wish to install a young child.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui further reported: "Rong fears that Your Majesty will ultimately become this threat. If there is a crown prince, he will greedily seek to install a young child instead.

sentences.zh: 若皇后不生太子，則立陳留以安天下。

translations.literal: If the empress does not bear a crown prince, then install Chenliu to settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If the empress does not bear a crown prince, he would install Chenliu to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 」並言榮指陳留語狀。

translations.literal: " He also reported Rong's words in pointing at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: " He also reported what Rong had said while pointing at Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 帝既有圖榮意，夜夢手持一刀自害，落十指節，都不覺痛。

translations.literal: The emperor, already intending to destroy Rong, dreamed at night that he held a knife and harmed himself, severing the joints of ten fingers, yet felt no pain at all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang, already intent on destroying Rong, dreamed one night that he held a knife and cut himself, severing the joints of all ten fingers, yet felt no pain at all.

sentences.zh: 惡之，以告城陽王徽及楊侃。

translations.literal: He found it ominous and told the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, and Yang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He found the dream ominous and told the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, and Yang Kan.

sentences.zh: 徽解夢曰：「蝮蛇螫手，壯士解腕。

translations.literal: Hui interpreted the dream: "When a viper bites the hand, the brave man severs his wrist.
translations.idiomatic: Hui interpreted the dream: "When a viper bites the hand, the brave man severs his wrist.

sentences.zh: 割指節與解腕何異？

translations.literal: How is cutting off finger joints different from severing the wrist?
translations.idiomatic: How is cutting off finger joints different from severing the wrist?

sentences.zh: 去患乃是吉祥。

translations.literal: Removing the affliction is itself auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the affliction is itself auspicious.

sentences.zh: 」聞者皆言善。

translations.literal: " All who heard said it was well said.
translations.idiomatic: " All who heard said he had spoken well.

sentences.zh: 九月十五日，天穆到京，駕迎之。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month, Tianmu reached the capital, and the imperial carriage went to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month, Yuan Tianmu reached the capital, and the imperial carriage went out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 榮與天穆並從入西林園燕射。

translations.literal: Rong and Tianmu both followed in and entered the Western Grove Garden for a feast and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Tianmu both followed in and entered the Western Grove Garden for a feast and archery contest.

sentences.zh: 榮乃奏曰：「近來侍官皆不習武，陛下宜將五百騎出獵，因省辭訟。

translations.literal: Rong then memorialized: "Recently attendants are all untrained in martial arts; Your Majesty ought to take five hundred cavalry out hunting and thereby review litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then memorialized: "Recently the attendants are all untrained in martial arts. Your Majesty ought to take five hundred cavalry out hunting and thereby review legal cases.

sentences.zh: 」先是奚毅言榮因獵挾天子移都，至是，其言相符。

translations.literal: " Earlier Xi Yi had said Rong would use the hunt to take the Son of Heaven hostage and move the capital—now his words matched.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Xi Yi had said Rong would use the hunt to take the Son of Heaven hostage and move the capital—now his words proved true.

sentences.zh: 至十八日，召中書舍人溫子升告以殺榮狀，並問以殺董卓事。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day, he summoned Secretariat Drafter Wen Zisheng and told him the plan to kill Rong, and also asked him about the killing of Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day, he summoned Secretariat Drafter Wen Zisheng, told him the plan to kill Rong, and also asked him about the killing of Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 子升具通本，上曰：「王允若即赦涼州人，必不應至此。

translations.literal: Zisheng fully related the original account; the emperor said: "If Wang Yun had immediately pardoned the Liangzhou men, it would certainly not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng related the whole story. Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "If Wang Yun had immediately pardoned the Liangzhou men, it would certainly not have come to this.

sentences.zh: 」良久，語子升曰：「朕之情理，卿所具知，死猶須為，況必不死！

translations.literal: " After a long while, he said to Zisheng: "Our feelings and reasoning, which you fully know—death must still be risked, and how much more when death is not certain!
translations.idiomatic: " After a long silence, he said to Zisheng: "You know my feelings and reasoning full well. The deed must be done even if death is certain—and how much more when death is not!

sentences.zh: 甯與高貴鄉公同日死，不與常道鄉公同日生。

translations.literal: Better to die on the same day as the Duke of Gaogu District than to live on the same day as the Duke of Changdao District.
translations.idiomatic: Better to die on the same day as the Duke of Gaogu District than to live on the same day as the Duke of Changdao District.

sentences.zh: 」上謂殺榮、天穆，即赦其党，便應不動。

translations.literal: " The emperor believed that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their faction immediately pardoned, there should be no disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor believed that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their faction immediately pardoned, the realm would remain calm.

sentences.zh: 應詔王道習曰：「尒硃世隆、司馬子如、硃元龍比來偏被委付，具知天下虛實，謂不宜留。

translations.literal: Yingzhao Wang Daoxi said: "Erzhu Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong have recently been especially entrusted with authority; they know the whole realm's strengths and weaknesses, and it is said they should not be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhao Wang Daoxi said: "Erzhu Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong have lately been especially entrusted with power; they know the realm's strengths and weaknesses through and through, and I say they should not be spared.

sentences.zh: 」城陽王及楊侃曰：「若世隆不全，仲遠、天光豈有來理？

translations.literal: " The Prince of Chengyang and Yang Kan said: "If Shilong were not kept alive whole, would Zhongyuan and Tianguang have any reason to come?
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Chengyang and Yang Kan said: "If Shilong is not kept alive and whole, what reason would Zhongyuan and Tianguang have to come?

sentences.zh: 」帝亦謂然，無復殺意。

translations.literal: " The emperor also considered this correct and no longer had intent to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaozhuang agreed and no longer intended to kill them.

sentences.zh: 城陽曰：「榮數征伐，腰間有刀，或能狠戾傷人。

translations.literal: Chengyang said: "Rong has fought many campaigns; there is a knife at his waist, and he might violently harm someone.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chengyang said: "Rong has fought in many campaigns. He carries a knife at his waist and might turn violent and harm someone.

sentences.zh: 臨事，願陛下出。

translations.literal: When the deed is at hand, I wish Your Majesty would withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment comes, I ask that Your Majesty withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」乃伏侃等十餘人於明光殿東。

translations.literal: " They then hid Kan and more than ten others east of the Hall of Bright Light.
translations.idiomatic: " They then hid Kan and more than ten others east of the Hall of Bright Light.

sentences.zh: 其日，榮與天穆併入，坐食未訖，起出。

translations.literal: That day Rong and Tianmu entered together; they had not finished sitting and eating when they rose and left.
translations.idiomatic: That day Rong and Tianmu entered together. They had not finished their meal when they rose and left.

sentences.zh: 侃等從東階上殿，見榮、天穆出至中庭，事不果。

translations.literal: Kan and the others ascended the hall from the eastern stairs; they saw Rong and Tianmu had gone out to the central courtyard—the affair came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Kan and the others rushed up the eastern stairs, but saw Rong and Tianmu already out in the central courtyard—the attempt came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 十九日是帝忌日。

translations.literal: The nineteenth was the emperor's mourning day.
translations.idiomatic: The nineteenth was the emperor's day of mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十日榮忌日。

translations.literal: The twentieth was Rong's mourning day.
translations.idiomatic: The twentieth was Rong's day of mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，暫入，即向陳留王家，飲酒極醉。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first, he briefly entered, then went straight to the Chenliu princely house and drank until utterly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first, Rong briefly entered court, then went straight to the Chenliu princely house and drank until utterly drunk.

sentences.zh: 遂言病動，頻日不入。

translations.literal: He then claimed his illness was acting up and for days did not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: He then claimed his old illness was flaring up and for several days did not enter court.

sentences.zh: 上謀頗泄，世隆等以告榮。

translations.literal: The emperor's plot leaked considerably; Shilong and the others told Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's plot leaked badly, and Shilong and the others told Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮輕帝，不謂能反。

translations.literal: Rong looked down on the emperor and did not think he could rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Rong looked down on the emperor and did not think him capable of striking back.

sentences.zh: 預帝謀者皆懼。

translations.literal: All who shared in the emperor's plot were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: All who shared in the emperor's plot were terrified.

sentences.zh: 二十五日旦，榮、天穆同入，其日大欲革易。

translations.literal: On the morning of the twenty-fifth, Rong and Tianmu entered together; that day there was strong intent to effect a great change.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of the twenty-fifth, Rong and Tianmu entered together—the day on which the great change was to be carried out.

sentences.zh: 上在明光殿東序中西面坐，榮與天穆並御床西北小床上南坐，城陽入，始一拜。

translations.literal: The emperor sat facing west in the western wing of the eastern sequence of the Hall of Bright Light; Rong and Tianmu both sat facing south on small beds northwest of the imperial couch; when Chengyang entered, he began with only one bow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang sat facing west in the western wing of the Hall of Bright Light's eastern gallery. Rong and Tianmu both sat facing south on low couches northwest of the imperial couch. When the Prince of Chengyang entered, he offered only a single bow.

sentences.zh: 榮見光祿卿魯安等持刀從東戶入，即馳向御坐，帝拔千牛刀，手斬之，時年三十八。

translations.literal: When Rong saw Grand Master of Splendor Lu An and others enter through the eastern gate holding knives, he immediately rushed toward the imperial seat; the emperor drew his Qianniu sword and personally beheaded him—he was thirty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong saw Grand Master of Splendor Lu An and others enter through the eastern gate with drawn blades, he rushed toward the imperial seat. Emperor Xiaozhuang drew his imperial sword and struck off his head with his own hand. Rong was thirty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 得其手板上有數牒啟，皆左右去留人名，非其腹心，悉在出限。

translations.literal: On his tally board were found several memorial slips listing names of attendants to be dismissed or retained; those who were not his close intimates were all marked for removal.
translations.idiomatic: On his tally board were found several slips listing names of attendants to be dismissed or retained; all who were not his close intimates were marked for removal.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豎子！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Vile whelp!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang said: "Vile whelp!

sentences.zh: 若過今日，便不可制。

translations.literal: If he had passed beyond today, he could not have been controlled.
translations.idiomatic: If he had lived beyond today, he could no longer have been controlled.

sentences.zh: 」時又天穆與榮子菩提亦就戮，於是內外喜叫，聲滿京城。

translations.literal: " At the same time Tianmu and Rong's son Puti were also executed; then within and without erupted in joyous shouting that filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " At the same time Yuan Tianmu and Rong's son Puti were also executed. Joyous shouts erupted inside and outside the palace, filling the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而大赦。

translations.literal: Soon after, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 榮雖威名大振，而舉止輕脫，止以馳射為伎藝，每入朝見，更無所為，唯戲上下馬。

translations.literal: Though Rong's martial renown was greatly magnified, his conduct was frivolous and rash; he valued only horsemanship and archery as skills; each time he entered court audience he did nothing else, only played at mounting and dismounting.
translations.idiomatic: Though Erzhu Rong's martial renown was immense, his bearing was frivolous and rash. Horsemanship and archery were his only real skills. Each time he entered court audience he did nothing of substance, only amused himself by mounting and dismounting his horse.

sentences.zh: 于西林園宴射，恆請皇后出觀，並召王公妃主，共在一堂。

translations.literal: At the Western Grove Park he held feasts with archery contests, constantly asking the empress to come out and watch, and summoning princes, dukes, imperial consorts, and princesses to share one hall together.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Grove Park he held feasting and archery contests, constantly asking the empress to come out and watch, and summoning princes, dukes, imperial consorts, and princesses to gather in a single hall.

sentences.zh: 每見天子射中，輒自起舞叫，將相卿士，悉皆盤旋，乃至妃主婦人，亦不免隨之舉袂。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw the Son of Heaven hit the target, he would at once rise to dance and shout; generals, ministers, and grandees all whirled about, and even imperial consorts and ladies could not avoid raising their sleeves and joining in.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw Emperor Xiaozhuang hit the target, he would leap up dancing and shouting. Generals, ministers, and grandees all spun about in turn, and even imperial consorts and court ladies could not help raising their sleeves and joining in.

sentences.zh: 及酒酣耳熱，必自匡坐，唱虜歌，為《樹梨普梨》之曲。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone to his head and his ears burned hot, he would invariably sit upright himself, sing barbarian songs, and perform the tune "Shuli Puli."
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone to his head and flushed his ears, he would sit bolt upright and sing barbarian songs, performing the tune "Shuli Puli."

sentences.zh: 見臨淮王彧從容閒雅，愛尚風素，固令為敕勒舞。

translations.literal: Seeing Prince Linhuai Yu composed, leisurely, and elegant, fond of simple refinement, he insisted that he perform the Tiele dance.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Prince Linhuai Yu composed and refined, a man who loved plain elegance, Erzhu Rong insisted that he perform the Tiele dance.

sentences.zh: 日暮罷歸，便與左右聯手蹋地，唱《回波樂》而出。

translations.literal: At day's end, when the gathering broke up and he returned, he would join hands with his attendants, stamp the ground, and go out singing "Returning Waves."
translations.idiomatic: At day's end, when the gathering broke up and he went home, he would join hands with his attendants, stamp the ground in rhythm, and leave singing "Returning Waves."

sentences.zh: 性甚嚴暴，慍喜無恆，弓箭刀槊，不離於手，每有瞋嫌，即行忍害，左右恆有死憂。

translations.literal: His nature was extremely stern and violent; anger and joy had no constancy; bow, arrows, knife, and spear never left his hand; whenever he felt resentment, he immediately carried out cruel harm; those around him constantly lived in fear of death.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was savagely violent, his moods utterly unpredictable. Bow, arrows, knife, and spear never left his hand. At the slightest grievance he would kill on the spot, and those around him lived in constant dread of death.

sentences.zh: 曾欲出獵，有人訴之，披陳不已，發怒，即射殺之。

translations.literal: Once when he wished to go out hunting, someone came to plead a case and laid out the grievance without stopping; enraged, he immediately shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he was about to go hunting, a man came to plead a case and would not stop presenting his grievance. Enraged, Erzhu Rong shot him dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 曾見沙彌重騎一馬，榮即令相觸，力窮不復能動，遂使傍人以頭相擊，死而後已。

translations.literal: Once he saw a novice monk heavily mounted on one horse; Rong immediately ordered them to charge each other; when their strength was exhausted and they could no longer move, he then had those standing by strike each other's heads until they died.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw a novice monk riding a heavily laden horse. Erzhu Rong ordered the horses to charge each other. When both beasts were spent and could no longer move, he had bystanders bash the riders' heads together until they were dead.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，世隆等得志，乃詔贈假黃鉞、相國、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事、晉王，加九錫，給九旒鑾輅，武賁班劍三百人，轀輬車，准晉太宰、安平獻王故事，諡曰武。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiemin Emperor's reign, when Shilong and the others had gained their wish, an edict posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, and Prince of Jin; added the Nine Bestowments; granted the nine-tassel imperial carriage, three hundred guards with ceremonial swords, and the imperial hearse; following the precedent of the Jin Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Anping, Xian; posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiemin Emperor's reign, after Erzhu Shilong and his faction had gained power, an edict posthumously invested Erzhu Rong with the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, the Chancellorship, the directorship of the Masters of Writing, supreme command over all armies at home and abroad, and the title Prince of Jin. He was granted the Nine Bestowments, the nine-tassel imperial carriage, three hundred guards bearing ceremonial swords, and an imperial hearse, following the precedent set for the Jin Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Anping. His posthumous title was Wu.

sentences.zh: 又詔百官議榮配饗，司直劉季明曰：「晉王若配永安，則不能終臣節。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered the hundred officials to deliberate on Rong's inclusion in ancestral offerings; Direct Censor Liu Jiming said: "If the Prince of Jin is paired with Yong'an, he cannot to the end fulfill the integrity of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered the officials to deliberate on pairing Erzhu Rong in the ancestral temple. Direct Censor Liu Jiming said: "If the Prince of Jin is paired with Yong'an, he cannot to the end fulfill the integrity of a loyal subject.

sentences.zh: 以此論之，無所配。

translations.literal: Judging by this, there is none with whom he may be paired.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by that, there is no emperor with whom he may properly be paired.

sentences.zh: 」世隆作色曰：「卿合配？

translations.literal: " Shilong changed expression and said: "Would you be the one to pair with him?
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Shilong's expression darkened. "Would you be the one to pair with him?

sentences.zh: 」季明曰：「下官預在議限，據理而言，不合上心，誅翦唯命。

translations.literal: " Jiming said: "This humble official was included within the limits of deliberation; speaking according to reason, if it does not accord with Your Excellency's wish, execution is yours to command.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Jiming said: "I was included in this deliberation. I spoke according to reason. If that does not please you, I accept execution at your command."

sentences.zh: 」眾為之危，季明自若。

translations.literal: " The assembly feared for him, but Jiming was composed as before.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly feared for him, but Liu Jiming remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 世隆意不已，乃配享孝文廟庭。

translations.literal: Shilong's intent was not yet satisfied, so he was paired for worship in the court of Emperor Xiaowen's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong was still not satisfied, and so had Erzhu Rong paired for worship in the court of Emperor Xiaowen's temple.

sentences.zh: 菩提位太常卿、開府儀同三司、侍中、特進。

translations.literal: Bodhi held the posts of Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand General with the privilege of an independent office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, and Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: Bodhi held the posts of Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand General with an independent office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, and Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 死時年十四。

translations.literal: At death he was fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fourteen when he died.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，加贈司徒，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiemin Emperor's reign, he was further posthumously granted Minister of Education; posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiemin Emperor's reign, he was further posthumously granted Minister of Education. His posthumous title was Hui.

sentences.zh: 菩提弟叉羅，武衛將軍、梁郡王。

translations.literal: Bodhi's younger brother Chaluo was General of Martial Guards and Prince of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bodhi's younger brother Chaluo was General of Martial Guards and Prince of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尒硃文暢

translations.literal: Erzhu Wenchang
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Wenchang

sentences.zh: 尒硃文略

translations.literal: Erzhu Wenlue
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Wenlue

sentences.zh: 弟文略，以兄叉羅卒無後，襲叉羅爵梁郡王。

translations.literal: The younger brother Wenlue, because his elder brother Chaluo died without heirs, inherited Chaluo's title as Prince of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Erzhu Wenlue, because his elder brother Chaluo died without heirs, inherited Chaluo's title as Prince of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 文暢事當從坐，靜帝使人往晉陽，欲拉殺之。

translations.literal: Wenchang's affair made him liable to joint punishment; the Jing Emperor sent men to Jinyang intending to strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Wenchang was liable to joint punishment for the affair, and the Jing Emperor sent men to Jinyang intending to strangle him to death.

sentences.zh: 神武特加寬貸，奏免之。

translations.literal: Shenwu specially granted leniency and memorialized to exempt him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan specially granted him leniency and memorialized to have the sentence waived.

sentences.zh: 文略聰明俊爽，多所通習。

translations.literal: Wenlue was intelligent, brilliant, and sharp, and was broadly versed in many things.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Wenlue was brilliant and quick-witted, broadly accomplished in many arts.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄嘗令章永興馬上彈琵琶，奏十餘曲，試使文略寫之，遂得八。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback, performing more than ten pieces; he tested Wenlue by having him write them down, and Wenlue got eight.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wenxiang once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback and perform more than ten pieces. He tested Erzhu Wenlue by having him transcribe them, and Wenlue reproduced eight.

sentences.zh: 文襄戲之曰：「聰明人多不老壽，梁郡其慎之！

translations.literal: Wenxiang teased him, saying: "Clever men often do not live to old age—Prince of Liang Commandery, take care!
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang teased him, saying: "Clever men often do not live to old age. Prince of Liang Commandery, take care!

sentences.zh: 」文略對曰：「命之修短，皆在明公。

translations.literal: " Wenlue replied: "Whether life is long or short—all lies with Your Excellency.
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Wenlue replied: "Whether life is long or short—all lies with Your Excellency."

sentences.zh: 」文襄愴然曰：「此不足慮。

translations.literal: " Wenxiang said mournfully: "That is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenxiang said with sudden sadness: "That is nothing to worry about."

sentences.zh: 」初，神武遣令恕文略十死，恃此益橫，多所陵忽。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Shenwu had left instructions to pardon Wenlue ten times from death; relying on this he became all the more overbearing and frequently insulted and slighted others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Huan had left instructions to pardon Erzhu Wenlue ten times from death. Relying on this, Wenlue grew ever more overbearing and frequently insulted and slighted others.

sentences.zh: 齊天保末，嘗邀平秦、武興、汝南諸王至宅，供設奢麗，各有贈賄。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi Tianbao, he once invited the princes of Pingqin, Wuxing, and Runan to his residence, providing lavish entertainment and giving each gifts and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qi Tianbao reign, he once invited the princes of Pingqin, Wuxing, and Runan to his residence, entertained them lavishly, and gave each gifts and bribes.

sentences.zh: 諸王共假聚寶物以要之，文略弊衣而往，從奴五十人，皆駿馬侯服。

translations.literal: The princes together borrowed and assembled treasures to impress him; Wenlue went in worn clothes, with fifty attendant slaves, all on fine horses and in princely dress.
translations.idiomatic: The princes pooled borrowed treasures to impress him. Erzhu Wenlue arrived in shabby clothes, attended by fifty slaves on fine horses and dressed in princely garb.

sentences.zh: 其豪縱不遜如此。

translations.literal: His arrogant insolence was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the height of his arrogant insolence.

sentences.zh: 平秦王有七百里馬，文略敵以好婢，賭取之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingqin had a horse that could run seven hundred li; Wenlue matched it with a fine maidservant and won it by gambling.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingqin owned a horse that could run seven hundred li in a day. Erzhu Wenlue wagered a fine maidservant against it and won the horse by gambling.

sentences.zh: 明日，平秦王使人致請，文略殺馬及婢，以二銀器盛婢頭馬肉而遺之。

translations.literal: The next day the Prince of Pingqin sent men to request their return; Wenlue killed the horse and the maidservant, placed the maidservant's head and the horse's flesh in two silver vessels, and sent them to him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Prince of Pingqin sent men to demand them back. Erzhu Wenlue slaughtered the horse and the maidservant, placed the maidservant's head and the horse's flesh in two silver vessels, and sent them to him.

sentences.zh: 平秦王訴之于文宣，系於京畿獄。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingqin complained to Wenxuan, and Wenlue was imprisoned in the capital prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingqin complained to Emperor Wenxuan, and Erzhu Wenlue was imprisoned in the capital prison.

sentences.zh: 文略彈琵琶，吹橫笛，謠詠倦極，便臥唱挽輓歌歌。

translations.literal: Wenlue played the pipa, blew the transverse flute, sang ballads until utterly weary, then lay down and sang dirges.
translations.idiomatic: In prison Erzhu Wenlue played the pipa, blew the transverse flute, and sang ballads until utterly weary, then lay down and sang dirges.

sentences.zh: 居數月，奪防者弓矢以射人，曰：「不然，天子不憶我。

translations.literal: After several months, he seized the guards' bow and arrows to shoot at people, saying: "If not, the Son of Heaven will not remember me.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he seized the guards' bow and arrows and shot at people, saying: "Otherwise the Son of Heaven will never remember me."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏，遂伏法。

translations.literal: " The responsible officials memorialized, and he was then executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為父作佳傳，收論榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。

translations.literal: Wenlue once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold, asking him to write a fine biography of his father; Shou compared Rong to Wei, Peng, Yi, and Huo—probably because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Wenlue once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father. Wei Shou's comparison of Erzhu Rong to Wei Zuo, Peng Zu, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was probably because of this.

sentences.zh: 尒硃兆

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao

sentences.zh: 兆字萬仁，榮從子也。

translations.literal: Zhao, courtesy name Wanren, was Rong's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, courtesy name Wanren, was Erzhu Rong's nephew.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，趫捷過人，數從榮遊獵，至窮岩絕澗，人所不能升降者，兆必先之。

translations.literal: From youth he excelled at horsemanship and archery, swift and agile beyond others; he often followed Rong on hunting excursions; reaching sheer cliffs and sheer ravines where others could not ascend or descend, Zhao always went first.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Erzhu Zhao excelled at horsemanship and archery, swifter and more agile than any other man. He often accompanied Erzhu Rong on hunting excursions. At sheer cliffs and bottomless ravines where others could not go up or down, Zhao always went first.

sentences.zh: 手格猛獸，無所疑避。

translations.literal: With his hands he grappled fierce beasts, never hesitating or shrinking.
translations.idiomatic: He grappled fierce beasts with his bare hands, never hesitating or shrinking.

sentences.zh: 榮以此特加賞愛，任為爪牙。

translations.literal: Rong for this reason specially favored and cherished him, employing him as a claw and fang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong for this reason favored him all the more and employed him as his strong right hand.

sentences.zh: 榮曾送台使，見二鹿，授兆二箭，令取供今食。

translations.literal: Rong once was seeing off an envoy from the capital; he saw two deer, gave Zhao two arrows, and ordered him to take them to supply today's meal.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while seeing off an envoy from the capital, Erzhu Rong saw two deer. He gave Erzhu Zhao two arrows and ordered him to bring them back for the day's meal.

sentences.zh: 遂構火以待之。

translations.literal: He then built a fire and waited for him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong then built a fire and waited.

sentences.zh: 俄而兆獲其一，榮欲誇使人，責兆不盡取，杖之五十。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao got one; Rong wished to boast before the envoy, blamed Zhao for not taking them all, and beat him fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Zhao brought back one. Wanting to boast before the envoy, Erzhu Rong blamed Zhao for not taking both and had him beaten fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 榮之入洛，兆兼前鋒都督。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Zhao also served as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Erzhu Zhao also served as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 孝莊即位，封潁川郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang acceded, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang acceded, Erzhu Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後從上党王天穆平邢杲。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Prince of Shangdang, Tianmu, in pacifying Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, in pacifying the rebel Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 又與賀拔勝擊斬元顥子冠受，禽之。

translations.literal: Again with Heba Sheng he attacked and struck down Yuan Hao's son Guanshou and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Heba Sheng in defeating and capturing Guanshou, son of Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 進破安豐王延明，顥乃退走。

translations.literal: Advancing, he defeated the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, and Hao then withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing further, he defeated the Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, and Yuan Hao then withdrew in flight.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，論功除車騎大將軍、儀同三司、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, for merit he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand General with the privilege of an independent office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Erzhu Zhao was rewarded with appointment as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand General with an independent office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮死，兆自汾州據晉陽。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Zhao from Fenzhou seized Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Zhao seized Jinyang from his base in Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，授兆大將軍，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established, Zhao was granted Grand General and advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Erzhu Zhao was granted the title Grand General and advanced in rank to prince.

sentences.zh: 兆與世隆等定謀攻洛。

translations.literal: Zhao with Shilong and the others settled on a plan to attack Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao joined Erzhu Shilong and the others in a plan to attack Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 兆遂輕兵倍道，掩襲京邑。

translations.literal: Zhao then with light troops doubled the march and made a surprise attack on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao then led light troops at forced march and made a surprise attack on the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，河邊人夢神謂己曰：「尒硃家欲度河，用爾作灅波津令，為之縮水脈。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man by the river dreamed that a god said to him: "The Erzhu family wishes to cross the river; they will use you as magistrate of Luobo Ford to shrink the water's course for them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man living by the river dreamed that a god said to him: "The Erzhu family wishes to cross the river. They will use you as magistrate of Luobo Ford to shrink the water's course for them.

sentences.zh: 」月餘，夢者死。

translations.literal: " After a little more than a month, the dreamer died.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a month later, the dreamer died.

sentences.zh: 及兆至，有行人自言知水淺處，以草往往表插而導焉，忽失其所在。

translations.literal: When Zhao arrived, a traveler said of himself that he knew where the water was shallow; he marked the way by sticking grass here and there to guide them, then suddenly vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao arrived, a traveler claimed to know where the water was shallow. He marked the way by sticking tufts of grass here and there to guide them, then suddenly vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 兆遂策馬涉度。

translations.literal: Zhao then spurred his horse and waded across.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao then spurred his horse and waded across.

sentences.zh: 是日暴風鼓怒，黃塵張天，騎叩宮門，宿衛乃覺。

translations.literal: That day a violent wind roared, yellow dust filled the sky, horsemen knocked on the palace gates, and only then did the palace guards become aware.
translations.idiomatic: That day a violent wind roared and yellow dust filled the sky. Horsemen knocked on the palace gates before the palace guards even realized what was happening.

sentences.zh: 彎弓欲射，袍撥弦，矢不得發，一時散走。

translations.literal: They bent bows intending to shoot, but their robes caught the bowstrings and the arrows could not be released; all at once they scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They bent their bows to shoot, but their robes caught the bowstrings and the arrows would not fly. In an instant they scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 莊帝步出雲龍門外，為兆騎所擊，幽于永寧佛寺。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang walked out beyond the Cloud Dragon Gate, was struck by Zhao's horsemen, and was confined in Yongning Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang walked out beyond the Cloud Dragon Gate, was seized by Erzhu Zhao's horsemen, and confined in Yongning Buddhist Temple.

sentences.zh: 兆撲殺皇子，汙辱妃嬪，縱兵虜掠。

translations.literal: Zhao beat imperial sons to death, defiled imperial consorts, and let his troops plunder and carry off booty.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao beat imperial princes to death, violated imperial consorts, and let his troops plunder the city.

sentences.zh: 停洛旬余，先令衛送莊帝于晉陽，兆後於河梁監閱財貨。

translations.literal: He remained in Luoyang for more than ten days; first he ordered guards to escort Emperor Xiaozhuang to Jinyang; Zhao afterward at the River Bridge supervised and inspected goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Luoyang for more than ten days. First he ordered guards to escort Emperor Xiaozhuang to Jinyang, while Erzhu Zhao himself stayed behind at the River Bridge to supervise the plunder.

sentences.zh: 初，兆將入洛，遣使招齊神武，欲與同舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao was about to enter Luoyang, he sent envoys to summon Qi Shenwu, wishing to rise together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Erzhu Zhao was about to enter Luoyang, he sent envoys to summon Gao Huan, wishing to rise together with him.

sentences.zh: 神武時為晉州刺史，謂長史孫騰曰：「臣而伐君，其逆已甚。

translations.literal: Shenwu was then Governor of Jinzhou; he said to Chief Clerk Sun Teng: "A subject attacking his ruler—the rebellion is already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was then Governor of Jinzhou. He said to Chief Clerk Sun Teng: "A subject attacking his ruler—that rebellion is already extreme.

sentences.zh: 我今不往，恐彼致恨，卿可往申吾意，但雲山蜀未平，不可委去。

translations.literal: If I do not go now, I fear they will bear resentment; you may go and explain my intent, only saying that the mountains of Shu are not yet pacified and I cannot leave my post.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not go now, I fear they will resent me. You may go and explain my intent, saying only that the mountains of Shu are not yet pacified and I cannot leave my post.

sentences.zh: 」騰乃詣兆，具申意。

translations.literal: " Teng then went to Zhao and fully explained the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng then went to Erzhu Zhao and fully explained Gao Huan's intent.

sentences.zh: 兆不悅，曰：「還白高兄弟，有吉夢，今行必克。

translations.literal: Zhao was displeased and said: "Go back and tell Brother Gao: I had an auspicious dream; if I go now, I am certain to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was displeased and said: "Go back and tell Brother Gao: I had an auspicious dream. If I march now, I am certain to prevail.

sentences.zh: 吾比夢吾亡父登一高堆，堆傍地悉耕熟，唯有馬蘭草株，往往猶在，吾父顧我，令下拔之。

translations.literal: Recently I dreamed that my dead father climbed a high mound; the ground beside the mound was all plowed and ripe, only stalks of horse orchid grass here and there still remained; my father looked back at me and ordered me to go down and pull them up.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I dreamed that my dead father climbed a high mound. The ground beside the mound was all plowed and ripe, yet stalks of horse orchid grass still stood here and there. My father looked back at me and ordered me to go down and pull them up.

sentences.zh: 吾手所至，無不盡出。

translations.literal: Wherever my hand reached, none failed to come out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever my hand reached, every stalk came out by the roots.

sentences.zh: 以此而言，往必有利。

translations.literal: Speaking by this, going will surely be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: By that omen, the march is sure to succeed.

sentences.zh: 」騰還，具報之。

translations.literal: " Teng returned and fully reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng returned and reported all of this to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「兆等倡狂，舉兵犯順，吾勢不可反事尒硃也。

translations.literal: Shenwu said: "Zhao and the others are wildly reckless, raising troops in violation of right order; given my position, I cannot turn back to serve the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said: "Zhao and the others are wildly reckless, raising troops in violation of right order. For me, there can be no turning back to serve the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 今天子列兵河上，兆進不能度，必退還。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven has arrayed troops on the river; if Zhao advances and cannot cross, he is certain to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has arrayed troops on the river. If Zhao advances and cannot cross, he is certain to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 吾乘山東下，出其不意，此徒可一舉而禽。

translations.literal: I will ride down from the eastern mountains, take them unawares, and this band can be captured in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: I will ride down from the eastern mountains and take them unawares. That band can be captured in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 」俄而兆克京師，孝莊幽縶，都督尉景從兆南行，以書報神武。

translations.literal: " Before long Zhao took the capital; Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned; Commander Wei Jing followed Zhao south and reported by letter to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Zhao took the capital. Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned. Commander Wei Jing followed Zhao south and reported by letter to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武大驚，召騰，令馳驛詣兆，示以謁賀，密觀天子所在，當于路邀迎，唱大義於天下。

translations.literal: Shenwu was greatly alarmed; he summoned Teng and ordered him to ride post-haste to Zhao, show the appearance of paying respects in congratulation, secretly observe where the Son of Heaven was, and when on the road intercept and welcome him, proclaiming righteousness to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was greatly alarmed. He summoned Sun Teng and ordered him to ride post-haste to Erzhu Zhao, feign congratulations, secretly learn where the emperor was, intercept and welcome him on the road, and proclaim righteousness to the realm.

sentences.zh: 騰遇帝于中路，神武時率騎東轉，聞帝已度，於是西還。

translations.literal: Teng met the emperor on the middle stretch of the road; Shenwu at the time was leading horsemen turning east; hearing the emperor had already passed, he then turned back west.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng met the emperor midway. Gao Huan was then leading his horsemen eastward, but hearing that the emperor had already passed, he turned back west.

sentences.zh: 仍與兆書，具陳禍福，不宜害天子，受惡名於海內。

translations.literal: He then wrote to Zhao, fully setting forth fortune and disaster, that he ought not harm the Son of Heaven and incur an evil name throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Erzhu Zhao, fully setting forth the consequences, urging that he must not harm the Son of Heaven and incur infamy throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 兆怒不納，而帝遂遇弑。

translations.literal: Zhao in anger would not accept, and the emperor then met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao angrily refused, and the emperor was then assassinated.

sentences.zh: 初，榮既死，莊帝詔河西人紇豆陵步蕃等，令襲秀容。

translations.literal: Earlier, once Rong had died, Emperor Xiaozhuang edicted the Hexi man Qidouling Bufan and others to attack Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Erzhu Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang ordered the Hexi commander Qidouling Bufan and others to attack Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 兆入洛後，步蕃兵勢甚盛，南逼晉陽。

translations.literal: After Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's military strength was very great, pressing south toward Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's army grew very powerful and pressed south toward Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 兆所以不暇留洛，回師禦之。

translations.literal: The reason Zhao had no leisure to remain in Luoyang was that he turned his army back to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: That was why Erzhu Zhao could not linger in Luoyang and turned his army back to resist him.

sentences.zh: 頻為步蕃所敗，於是部勒士馬，謀出山東，令人頻徵神武。

translations.literal: Repeatedly defeated by Bufan, he then organized troops and horses, planned to go out toward the eastern mountains, and sent men repeatedly to summon Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly defeated by Bufan, he reorganized his troops and planned to move out toward the eastern mountains, sending men repeatedly to summon Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武晉州僚屬，並勸不行。

translations.literal: Shenwu's Jinzhou staff all urged him not to go.
translations.idiomatic: All of Gao Huan's staff in Jinzhou urged him not to go.

sentences.zh: 神武揣其勢迫，必無他慮，決策赴之。

translations.literal: Shenwu reckoned that with their situation pressed tight, they would certainly have no other designs, and decided to go to them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan reckoned that with their situation desperate, they would certainly have no other designs, and decided to go.

sentences.zh: 兆乃分三州六鎮之人，令神武統領。

translations.literal: Zhao then divided the people of the three provinces and six garrisons and ordered Shenwu to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao then placed the people of three provinces and six garrisons under Gao Huan's command.

sentences.zh: 神武既分兵別營，乃引兵南出，避步蕃之銳。

translations.literal: Once Shenwu had divided troops into separate camps, he then led troops south out, avoiding Bufan's sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Huan had divided his troops into separate camps, he led his army south, avoiding Bufan's main force.

sentences.zh: 步蕃至樂平郡，神武與兆還討，破斬之。

translations.literal: When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, Shenwu and Zhao turned back to attack him, defeated him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, Gao Huan and Erzhu Zhao turned back to attack him, defeated him, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 及節閔帝立，授兆使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、柱國大將軍，兼錄尚書事、大行台。

translations.literal: When the Jiemin Emperor was established, Zhao was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Pillar of State Grand General, concurrently Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiemin Emperor was enthroned, Erzhu Zhao was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme command over all armies at home and abroad, Pillar of State Grand General, and concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又以兆為天柱大將軍，兆以是榮所終之官，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Again Zhao was made Pillar of Heaven Grand General; because this was the office at which Rong ended, Zhao firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was also offered the title Pillar of Heaven Grand General, but because that was the last office Erzhu Rong had held, Zhao firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 尋加都督十州諸軍事，世襲并州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was further granted command over the armies of ten provinces, with hereditary succession as Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further granted command over the armies of ten provinces, with hereditary succession as Governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 神武之克殷州也，兆與仲遠、度律約拒之。

translations.literal: When Shenwu took Yinzhou, Zhao with Zhongyuan and Dulu agreed to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan took Yinzhou, Erzhu Zhao joined Zhongyuan and Dulu in an agreement to resist him.

sentences.zh: 仲遠、度律次陽平，兆屯廣阿，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and Dulu encamped at Yangping; Zhao stationed troops at Guang'a; their forces were said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and Dulu encamped at Yangping, Erzhu Zhao stationed his troops at Guang'a, and their combined forces were said to number one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 神武廣縱反間，於是兩不相信，各致猜疑。

translations.literal: Shenwu widely spread counter-intelligence, and thus the two sides no longer trusted each other, each arousing suspicion in the other.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan spread disinformation widely, and the two sides lost trust in each other, each growing suspicious of the other.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等頻使斛斯椿賀拔勝往喻之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others repeatedly sent Husi Chun and Heba Sheng to go and explain matters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and his allies repeatedly dispatched Husi Chun and Heba Sheng to reason with him.

sentences.zh: 兆輕騎三百，來就仲遠，同坐幕下。

translations.literal: Zhao came with three hundred light horsemen to join Zhongyuan; they sat together beneath the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao rode in with three hundred light cavalry to meet Zhongyuan, and the two sat together under the command tent.

sentences.zh: 兆性粗獷，意色不平，手舞馬鞭，長嘯凝望，深疑仲遠等有變，遂趨出馳還。

translations.literal: Zhao was coarse and rough by nature; his expression was unsettled. He waved a riding crop in his hand, gave a long whistling cry and stared into the distance, deeply suspecting that Zhongyuan and the others were plotting treachery, and rushed out and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was coarse and volatile by nature. His face dark with suspicion, he flourished his riding crop, gave a long whistle, and stared into the distance, convinced that Zhongyuan and the others meant to turn on him. He bolted from the tent and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣椿、勝等追而曉譬，兆遂拘縛將還，經日放遣。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent Chun, Sheng, and the others to pursue him and explain matters clearly. Zhao was then bound and brought back; after a day he was released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan sent Husi Chun, Heba Sheng, and others in pursuit to reason with him. Erzhu Zhao was seized, bound, and brought back, then released and sent off a day later.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等於是奔退。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others thereupon fled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and his forces thereupon broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 神武乃進擊，兆軍大敗。

translations.literal: Shenwu then pressed the attack, and Zhao's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then pressed the attack, and Erzhu Zhao's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 兆與仲遠、度律遂相疑阻，久而不和。

translations.literal: Zhao, Zhongyuan, and Dulu thereupon came to mutual suspicion and obstruction, and for a long time were not reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, Zhongyuan, and Dulu grew mutually suspicious and obstructive, and remained at odds for a long time.

sentences.zh: 世隆請節閔納兆女為皇后，兆乃大喜。

translations.literal: Shilong asked the Jiemin Emperor to take Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong persuaded the Jiemin Emperor to take Erzhu Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 世隆謀抗神武，乃降辭厚禮，喻兆赴洛。

translations.literal: Shilong plotted to resist Shenwu; he sent humble words and rich gifts to persuade Zhao to come to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong plotted to resist Gao Huan and sent humble messages and lavish gifts to coax Erzhu Zhao to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 兆與天光、度律更自信約，然後大會韓陵山。

translations.literal: Zhao, Tianguang, and Dulu renewed their covenant of trust, and then assembled in great force at Hanling Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Tianguang, and Dulu reaffirmed their alliance, then mustered their full strength at Hanling Mountain.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，復奔晉陽。

translations.literal: They were defeated in battle and again fled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: They were defeated in battle and again fled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，神武自鄴進討之，兆遂大掠并州，走于秀容。

translations.literal: That autumn, Shenwu marched from Ye to attack him. Zhao then plundered Bingzhou on a great scale and fled to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Gao Huan marched from Ye to attack him. Erzhu Zhao plundered Bingzhou on a vast scale and fled to Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 神武又追擊，度赤洪嶺，破之。

translations.literal: Shenwu pressed the pursuit again, crossed Red Hong Ridge, and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan pressed the pursuit again, crossed Red Hong Ridge, and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 兆竄於窮山，殺所乘馬，自縊於樹。

translations.literal: Zhao hid in a remote mountain, killed the horse he was riding, and hanged himself from a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao hid in a desolate mountain, killed his mount, and hanged himself from a tree.

sentences.zh: 神武收葬之。

translations.literal: Shenwu gathered his remains and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan recovered his body and gave him a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 兆勇於戰鬥，而無將領之能。

translations.literal: Zhao was brave in battle but lacked the capacity of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was fearless in combat but lacked the talent of a general.

sentences.zh: 榮雖奇其膽決，然每云：「兆不過將三千騎，多則亂矣。」

translations.literal: Rong though he admired his bold resolve, yet always said: "Zhao cannot command more than three thousand horsemen; with more, there is disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong admired his boldness, yet always said, "Zhao can lead no more than three thousand horsemen; give him more and everything falls apart."

sentences.zh: 兆弟智彪，節閔帝封為安定王。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Zhibiao was enfeoffed by the Jiemin Emperor as Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao's younger brother Zhibiao was enfeoffed by the Jiemin Emperor as Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 與兆俱走，神武禽之。

translations.literal: He fled together with Zhao; Shenwu captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He fled together with Erzhu Zhao and was captured by Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 後死于晉陽。

translations.literal: He later died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 尒硃彥伯

translations.literal: Erzhu Yanbo
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yanbo

sentences.zh: 彥伯，榮從弟也。

translations.literal: Yanbo was Rong's paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yanbo was Erzhu Rong's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖侯真，文成時並、安二州刺史、始昌侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hou Zhen, in the time of Emperor Wencheng, was Inspector of Bing and An prefectures and Marquis of Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hou Zhen had served under Emperor Wencheng as Inspector of Bing and An prefectures and as Marquis of Shichang.

sentences.zh: 父買珍，宣武時武衛將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Mai Zhen, in the time of Emperor Xuanwu, was General of the Military Guard and Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mai Zhen had served under Emperor Xuanwu as General of the Military Guard and Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 彥伯性和厚，永安中，為榮府長史。

translations.literal: Yanbo's nature was gentle and generous. In the Yong'an era he served as chief clerk in Rong's princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yanbo was mild and generous by nature. During the Yong'an era he served as chief clerk in Erzhu Rong's princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝潛嘿于龍花佛寺，彥伯敦喻往來，尤有勤款。

translations.literal: The Jiemin Emperor kept silent in seclusion at Longhua Buddhist Temple; Yanbo urged and explained matters back and forth, showing exceptional earnest devotion.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Jiemin Emperor lived in silent seclusion at Longhua Buddhist Temple, Erzhu Yanbo went back and forth urging and explaining matters to him with exceptional earnest devotion.

sentences.zh: 帝既立，尒硃兆以己不豫謀，大為忿恚，將攻世隆。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had been enthroned, Erzhu Zhao, because he had not participated in the plot, was greatly angry and resentful, and intended to attack Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had been enthroned, Erzhu Zhao, furious that he had not been included in the plot, intended to attack Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 詔令華山王鷙慰兆，兆猶不釋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Hua of Huashan to console Zhao, but Zhao still would not relent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince Hua of Huashan to placate Erzhu Zhao, but Zhao still would not be appeased.

sentences.zh: 世隆復令彥伯自往喻之，兆乃止。

translations.literal: Shilong again had Yanbo go in person to explain to him, and Zhao then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong again sent Erzhu Yanbo in person to reason with him, and Erzhu Zhao then desisted.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝宴彥伯于顯陽殿。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor gave Yanbo a banquet in the Hall of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo returned, the Jiemin Emperor gave him a banquet in the Hall of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 時侍中源子恭、黃門郎竇瑗並侍坐。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were both in attendance and seated.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were both in attendance.

sentences.zh: 彥伯曰：「源侍中比為都督，與臣相持於河內。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Attendant Yuan, you recently served as area commander and held against me at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yanbo said, "Attendant Yuan, you recently served as area commander and faced me in stalemate at Henei.

sentences.zh: 當爾之時，旗鼓相望，眇如天隔。

translations.literal: At that time our banners and drums faced each other across the distance, as though separated by heaven itself.
translations.idiomatic: In those days our banners and drums faced each other across the field, as though heaven itself lay between us.

sentences.zh: 甯期同事陛下，為今日之忻也？

translations.literal: Who could have expected we would serve the same sovereign and share today's joy?
translations.idiomatic: Who could have dreamed we would serve the same sovereign and share today's joy?

sentences.zh: 」子恭曰：「蒯通有言，犬吠非其主。

translations.literal: " Zigong said: "Kuai Tong once said, a dog barks not for its proper master.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Zigong said, "Kuai Tong once said that a dog barks not for its proper master.

sentences.zh: 他日之事永安，猶今日之事陛下耳。

translations.literal: What I did then for Yong'an is what I do today for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: What I did then in the service of Yong'an is what I do today in the service of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「源侍中可謂有射鉤之心也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Attendant Yuan may truly be said to have the heart that forgave the hook-shooter."
translations.idiomatic: " The Jiemin Emperor said, "Attendant Yuan may truly be said to have the heart that forgave the hook-shooter."

sentences.zh: 」遂令二人極醉而罷。

translations.literal: " They were then made to drink until utterly drunk, and the banquet ended.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had the two of them drink until utterly drunk, and the banquet ended.

sentences.zh: 後封博陵郡王，位司徒公。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling commandery and served as Duke of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling commandery and appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 于時炎旱，有勸彥伯解司徒者，乃上表遜位，詔許之。

translations.literal: At that time there was drought and heat; some urged Yanbo to resign as Minister over the Masses; he submitted a memorial yielding his post, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a severe drought afflicted the land. Some urged Erzhu Yanbo to resign as Minister over the Masses; he submitted a memorial yielding his post, and an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 俄除儀同三司、侍中，餘如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Yitong Sanqi and Palace Attendant; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Yitong Sanqi and Palace Attendant; his other privileges remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 彥伯于兄弟之中，差無過患。

translations.literal: Among the brothers, Yanbo was comparatively free of serious faults.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Erzhu brothers, Yanbo was comparatively free of serious faults.

sentences.zh: 天光等敗于韓陵，彥伯欲領兵屯河橋，世隆不從。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Yanbo wished to lead troops to hold the Heqiao Bridge; Shilong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Erzhu Yanbo wished to lead troops to hold the Heqiao Bridge, but Erzhu Shilong would not agree.

sentences.zh: 及張勸等掩襲世隆，彥伯時在禁直。

translations.literal: When Zhang Qu and the others launched a surprise attack on Shilong, Yanbo was then on night duty in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Qu and the others launched a surprise attack on Erzhu Shilong, Erzhu Yanbo was on night duty in the palace.

sentences.zh: 長孫承業等啟陳，神武義功既振，將除尒硃。

translations.literal: Changsun Chenye and the others submitted a memorial stating that Shenwu's righteous achievement had already gained momentum and he intended to eliminate the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Chenye and the others submitted a memorial stating that Gao Huan's righteous cause had already gained momentum and that he intended to eliminate the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 節閔令舍人郭崇報彥伯知，彥伯狼狽出走，為人所執。

translations.literal: The Jiemin Emperor ordered Attendant-of-the-Interior Guo Chong to inform Yanbo; Yanbo fled in disarray and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiemin Emperor ordered Attendant-of-the-Interior Guo Chong to warn Erzhu Yanbo. Yanbo fled in disarray and was seized.

sentences.zh: 尋與世隆同斬於閶闔門外，縣首於斛斯椿門樹，傳于神武。

translations.literal: Soon he was beheaded together with Shilong outside the Changhe Gate; his head was hung on the gate-tree at Husi Chun's residence and sent to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was beheaded together with Erzhu Shilong outside the Changhe Gate. His head was hung on the gate-tree at Husi Chun's residence and sent on to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 先是洛中謠曰：「三月末，四月初，揚灰簸土覓真珠。

translations.literal: Previously a song in Luoyang said: "At the end of the third month, in the early fourth month, winnow ash and sift dust searching for true pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a song in Luoyang had run: "At the end of the third month, in the early fourth month, winnow ash and sift dust searching for true pearls.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「頭去項，腳根齊，驅上樹，不須梯。

translations.literal: " Another said: "Head severed from the neck, feet level with the roots—drive him up a tree, no ladder needed."
translations.idiomatic: " Another ran: "Head severed from the neck, feet level with the roots—drive him up a tree, no ladder needed."

sentences.zh: 」至是並驗。

translations.literal: " When the time came, both were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: " When the time came, both prophecies were fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 子敞。

translations.literal: His son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Erzhu Chang.

sentences.zh: 尒硃敞

translations.literal: Erzhu Chang
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Chang

sentences.zh: 敞字乾羅。

translations.literal: Chang's style name was Qianluo.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Chang's style name was Qianluo.

sentences.zh: 彥伯之誅，敞小，隨母養于宮中。

translations.literal: When Yanbo was executed, Chang was young and was raised in the palace with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Yanbo was executed, Chang was still a child and was raised in the palace with his mother.

sentences.zh: 年十二，敞自竇走至大街，見童兒群戲，敞解所著綺羅金翠服，易衣而遁。

translations.literal: At age twelve, Chang slipped away through a hole in the wall to the main street, saw children playing in a group, stripped off the brocade silks and gold-emerald finery he was wearing, traded clothes, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, Chang slipped through a hole in the wall to the main street. Seeing a group of children at play, he stripped off his brocade silks and gold-emerald finery, traded clothes with one of them, and fled.

sentences.zh: 追騎至，不識敞，便執綺衣兒。

translations.literal: Pursuers arrived, did not recognize Chang, and seized the child in the brocade garments.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers arrived but did not recognize Chang; they seized the child in the brocade garments instead.

sentences.zh: 比究問知非，會日已暮，由是免。

translations.literal: When interrogation revealed it was not he, night had already fallen, and so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When interrogation showed they had the wrong child, night had already fallen, and so Chang escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 遂入一村，見長孫氏媼，踞胡床坐，敞再拜求哀，長孫氏湣之，藏於復壁之中。

translations.literal: He then entered a village, saw an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding chair, bowed twice begging mercy; the Changsun woman took pity on him and hid him in a hidden alcove.
translations.idiomatic: He entered a village and found an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding chair. Chang bowed twice in supplication; she took pity on him and hid him in a concealed alcove.

sentences.zh: 購之愈急，追且至，長孫氏資而遣之。

translations.literal: The bounty hunt grew more urgent and pursuers were nearly upon them; the Changsun woman supplied him with resources and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The manhunt grew fiercer and pursuers were nearly upon them. The Changsun woman gave him supplies and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 遂詐為道士，變姓名，隱嵩高山。

translations.literal: He then feigned being a Daoist priest, changed his name, and concealed himself on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed himself off as a Daoist priest, changed his name, and hid on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 略涉經史。

translations.literal: He dabbled in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He dabbled in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 數年間，人頗異之。

translations.literal: Over several years people found him rather unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Over several years people found him rather unusual.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨坐岩石下，泫然歎曰：「吾豈終此乎！

translations.literal: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed: "Am I to end my days like this!
translations.idiomatic: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed, "Am I to end my days like this!

sentences.zh: 伍子胥獨何人也？

translations.literal: What made Wu Zixu so special?
translations.idiomatic: What made Wu Zixu so special?

sentences.zh: 」乃奔長安。

translations.literal: " He then fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 周文帝見而禮之，拜行台郎中、靈壽縣伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou received him with honor, appointing him Langzhong of the mobile cabinet and Baron of Lingshou County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou received him with honor and appointed him Langzhong of the mobile cabinet and Baron of Lingshou County.

sentences.zh: 保定中，遷開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sanqi and advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sanqi and raised to the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 後為膠州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 迎長孫氏至其第，置於家，厚資給之。

translations.literal: He welcomed the Changsun woman to his residence, housed her in his home, and generously supported her.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the Changsun woman to his residence, housed her in his home, and supported her generously.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，改封邊城郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, his fief was changed to Duke of Biancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Chang's fief was changed to Duke of Biancheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 黔安蠻叛，命敞討平之。

translations.literal: The Qian'an barbarians rebelled; he was ordered to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qian'an tribes rebelled, he was ordered to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 師旋，拜金州總管，政號嚴明，吏人懼之。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Governor-General of Jinzhou; his governance was strict and clear, and officials and people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When his army returned he was appointed Governor-General of Jinzhou. His governance was strict and clear, and officials and commoners alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 後以年老乞骸骨，賜二馬輅車歸河內，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later, citing old age he requested retirement; he was granted a two-horse carriage and returned to Henei, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing old age, he requested retirement. He was granted a two-horse carriage, returned to Henei, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子最嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尒硃仲遠

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan

sentences.zh: 仲遠，彥伯弟也。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was Yanbo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was Erzhu Yanbo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 明帝末年，尒硃榮兵威稍盛，諸有啟謁，率多見從。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Ming, Erzhu Rong's military power gradually grew; most petitions and requests were approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Ming, Erzhu Rong's military power steadily grew, and most petitions and requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 而仲遠摹寫榮書，又刻榮印，與尚書令吏，通為奸詐。

translations.literal: Yet Zhongyuan copied Rong's letters and carved a seal in Rong's name, colluding with clerks of the Masters of Writing in fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan copied Erzhu Rong's letters and carved a seal in Rong's name, colluding with clerks of the Masters of Writing in fraud.

sentences.zh: 造榮啟表，請人為官，大得財貨，以資酒色。

translations.literal: He forged memorials in Rong's name to procure offices for people, reaping great wealth to fund wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: He forged memorials in Rong's name to procure offices for people, amassing great wealth to fund wine and women.

sentences.zh: 落魄無行業。

translations.literal: He was dissolute and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was dissolute and without proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊即位，封清河公、徐州刺史，兼尚書左僕射、三徐大行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe, made Inspector of Xuzhou, and concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Mobile Corps Commander of the Three Xus.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe, appointed Inspector of Xuzhou, and concurrently made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Mobile Corps Commander of the Three Xus.

sentences.zh: 尋進督三徐諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to oversee all military affairs of the Three Xus.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to oversee all military affairs of the Three Xus.

sentences.zh: 仲遠上言：「竊見比來行台采募者，皆得權立中正，在軍定第，斟酌授官。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan submitted a memorial: "I have observed that recently those recruiting troops through mobile corps have all been allowed to appoint local rankers on their own authority, fix grades within the army, and assign offices at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan submitted a memorial: "I observe that recently those recruiting troops through mobile corps have all been allowed to appoint local rankers on their own authority, fix grades within the army, and assign offices at discretion.

sentences.zh: 今求兼置，權濟軍要。

translations.literal: I now request to be granted the same authority to meet urgent military needs.
translations.idiomatic: I now request the same authority for myself, as a temporary measure to meet urgent military needs.

sentences.zh: 若立第亦爽，關京之日，任有司裁奪」。

translations.literal: If the grades I assign prove unsatisfactory, when the matter reaches the capital the responsible offices may revise them."
translations.idiomatic: If the grades I assign prove unsatisfactory, when the matter reaches the capital the responsible offices may revise them."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 於是隨情補授，肆意聚斂。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed offices as he pleased and extorted wealth without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon sold offices as he pleased and extorted wealth without restraint.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮死，仲遠勒其部眾，來向京師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Zhongyuan drove his troops and came toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Zhongyuan drove his troops toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 節閔立，進爵彭城王，加大將軍，又兼尚書令，鎮大梁。

translations.literal: When the Jiemin Emperor was enthroned, Zhongyuan was advanced to Prince of Pengcheng, given the title Grand General, and concurrently made Director of the Masters of Writing, stationed at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiemin Emperor was enthroned, Zhongyuan was advanced to Prince of Pengcheng, given the title Grand General, made Director of the Masters of Writing, and stationed at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣使請准朝式，在軍鳴騶。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent envoys requesting permission to follow court protocol and have outriders announce his passage while in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan sent envoys requesting permission to follow court protocol and have outriders announce his passage even while in the field.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝覽啟，笑而許之。

translations.literal: The Jiemin Emperor read the memorial, smiled, and approved it.
