translations.idiomatic: The Jiemin Emperor read the memorial, smiled, and granted it.

sentences.zh: 其肆情如此。

translations.literal: His self-indulgence was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent of his self-indulgence.

sentences.zh: 復進督東道諸軍事、本將軍、袞州刺史，余如故。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to oversee all military affairs of the Eastern Route, retained his original generalship, and was made Inspector of Yanzhou; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to oversee all military affairs of the Eastern Route, retained his original generalship, and was made Inspector of Yanzhou; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 仲遠天性貪暴，心如峻壑。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was greedy and violent by nature; his heart was like a steep ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was greedy and violent by nature; his heart was like a bottomless ravine.

sentences.zh: 大宗富族，誣之以反，沒其家口，簿籍財物，皆以入己。

translations.literal: Great clans and wealthy families he falsely accused of rebellion, confiscated their households, and recorded their goods and property—all for his own possession.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely accused great clans and wealthy families of rebellion, confiscated their households, and recorded their goods and property—all for his own possession.

sentences.zh: 丈夫死者，投之河流，如此者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Men who died were thrown into the river; such cases were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Men who died were thrown into the river; such cases were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 諸將婦有美色者，莫不被其淫亂。

translations.literal: Among the generals' wives who were beautiful, none escaped his debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: No beautiful wife among the generals escaped his debauchery.

sentences.zh: 自滎陽以東，輸稅悉入其軍，不送京師。

translations.literal: From Xingyang eastward, all tax deliveries went into his army and were not sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From Xingyang eastward, all tax deliveries went into his army and never reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 時天光控關右，仲遠在大梁，兆據并州，世隆居京邑，各自專恣，權強莫此。

translations.literal: At the time Tianguang controlled the lands west of the passes, Zhongyuan was at Daliang, Zhao held Bingzhou, and Shilong dwelt in the capital; each acted with unchecked will, and none wielded power more absolutely.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Erzhu Tianguang controlled the lands west of the passes, Zhongyuan held Daliang, Erzhu Zhao held Bingzhou, and Erzhu Shilong dwelt in the capital. Each ruled with unchecked will, and none wielded power more absolutely.

sentences.zh: 所在並以貪虐為事，於是四方解體。

translations.literal: Everywhere they made greed and cruelty their business, and thus the realm fell apart on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere they made greed and cruelty their business, and the realm began to fall apart on every side.

sentences.zh: 又加太宰，解大行台。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Grand Steward and relieved of the Grand Commandery Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Steward and stripped of his Grand Commandery Office.

sentences.zh: 仲遠專恣尤劇，方之彥伯、世隆，最為無禮。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's willfulness was especially extreme; compared with Yanbo and Shilong, he was the most disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan was the most unrestrained of the Erzhu clan—more arrogant and insolent even than Erzhu Yanbo and Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 東南牧守，下至人俗，比之豺狼，特為患苦。

translations.literal: From the regional governors of the southeast down to the common folk, they compared him to wolves and jackals; he was a particular source of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: From the governors of the southeast down to ordinary people, all compared him to wolves and jackals; he was a singular affliction.

sentences.zh: 後移屯東郡，率眾與度律等拒齊神武。

translations.literal: Later he moved his garrison to Dong commandery and led his troops with Dulu and others to resist Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He later shifted his camp to Dong commandery and led his forces with Erzhu Dulu and others to resist Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 尒硃兆領騎數千自晉陽來會。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao led several thousand horsemen from Jinyang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao rode in from Jinyang with several thousand cavalry to join the coalition.

sentences.zh: 軍次陽平，神武縱以間說，仲遠等迭相猜貳，狼狽遁走。

translations.literal: The army halted at Yangping. Gao Huan deployed agents to sow discord; Zhongyuan and the others grew mutually suspicious, and fled in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Yangping, Gao Huan sent agents to spread dissension. Erzhu Zhongyuan and his allies turned on one another in suspicion and fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，復與天光等於韓陵戰敗，南走。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, he was defeated again with Tianguang and others at Hanling and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he was defeated again with Erzhu Tianguang and the others at Hanling and fled south.

sentences.zh: 尋乃奔梁，死於江南。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he fled to Liang and died in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled to Liang and died in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 尒硃世隆

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong

sentences.zh: 世隆，字榮宗，仲遠弟也。

translations.literal: Shilong, style name Rongzong, was Zhongyuan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, whose style name was Rongzong, was Erzhu Zhongyuan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 明帝末，兼直閣，加前將軍。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Ming, he concurrently served in the Directorate of Attendants and was appointed Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of Emperor Ming's reign he served concurrently in the palace attendants corps and was appointed Forward General.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮表請入朝，靈太后惡之，令世隆詣晉陽慰喻榮。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong memorialized requesting entry to court; Empress Dowager Ling despised this and ordered Shilong to go to Jinyang to reassure Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong petitioned to enter the capital, Empress Dowager Ling was hostile to the idea and ordered Erzhu Shilong to Jinyang to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 榮因欲留之，世隆曰：「朝廷疑兄，故令世隆來。

translations.literal: Rong wished to detain him on this account. Shilong said, "The court suspects my brother, and therefore sent Shilong here.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong wanted to keep him there. Shilong said, "The court suspects my brother, and that is why they sent me.

sentences.zh: 今遂住，便有內備，非計之善。

translations.literal: If I stay now, there will be defensive preparations within the court—this is no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: If I remain, the court will take defensive measures at once. That would be a poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 」榮乃遣入。

translations.literal: Rong then sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong then let him proceed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 榮舉兵南出，世隆遂走，會榮於上黨。

translations.literal: When Rong raised troops and marched south, Shilong fled and joined Rong at Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched south at the head of his army, Shilong fled the capital and joined him at Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he was appointed Chief of the Yellow Gate Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Chief of the Yellow Gate Attendants.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之立，世隆預其謀，封樂平郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, Shilong participated in the plot and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, Shilong had taken part in the conspiracy and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping commandery.

sentences.zh: 元顥逼大梁，詔為前將軍、都督，鎮武牢。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed on Daliang, an edict made him Forward General and Area Commander, garrisoning Wu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao threatened Daliang, an edict appointed Shilong Forward General and Area Commander with orders to hold Wu Fort.

sentences.zh: 顥既克滎陽，世隆懼而遁還，莊帝倉卒北巡。

translations.literal: Once Yuan Hao had taken Xingyang, Shilong fled back in fear, and Emperor Xiaozhuang hastily toured north.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao captured Xingyang, Shilong fled in panic, and Emperor Xiaozhuang made a hurried northern retreat.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還宮，除尚書左僕射，攝選。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and acting Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Shilong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with acting authority over personnel appointments.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之將圖尒硃榮，每屏人言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was planning against Erzhu Rong, he would speak with attendants dismissed from the room.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Xiaozhuang plotted against Erzhu Rong, he would dismiss everyone from the room before speaking.

sentences.zh: 世隆懼變，乃為匿名書，自榜其門曰：「天子與侍中楊侃、黃門高道穆等為計，欲殺天柱。

translations.literal: Shilong feared change and wrote an anonymous letter, himself posting it on his gate: "The Son of Heaven with Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Kan, Huangmen Attendant Gao Daomu and others have plotted to kill the Heavenly Pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a coup, Shilong wrote an anonymous warning and posted it on his own gate: "The emperor, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Kan, Huangmen Attendant Gao Daomu, and others are plotting to kill the Heavenly Pillar.

sentences.zh: 」還復自以此書與榮妻北鄉郡公主，並以呈榮，勸其不入。

translations.literal: He also gave this letter to Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang commandery, and presented it to Rong as well, urging him not to enter.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the letter to Erzhu Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang commandery, and forwarded it to Rong himself, urging him not to enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 榮毀書唾地曰：「世隆無膽，誰敢生心！

translations.literal: Rong tore up the letter and spat on the ground, saying, "Shilong has no courage—who would dare harbor such a thought!
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong tore the letter to pieces and spat on the ground. "Shilong hasn't the nerve for this—who would dare raise a hand against me?

sentences.zh: 」世隆又勸其速發。

translations.literal: Shilong again urged him to depart quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong again urged him to leave at once.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「何忽忽？

translations.literal: Rong said, "Why such haste?
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong replied, "What's the hurry?

sentences.zh: 」皆不見從。

translations.literal: None of this was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored every warning.

sentences.zh: 榮死，世隆奉榮妻，燒西陽門夜走。

translations.literal: After Rong's death, Shilong attended Rong's wife, set fire to the Western Yang Gate, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Shilong escorted Rong's wife, set fire to the Western Yang Gate, and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 北次河橋，殺武衛將軍奚毅，率眾還戰大夏門外。

translations.literal: He halted north at River Bridge, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and led troops back to fight outside the Great Summer Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at River Bridge to the north, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and led his troops back to fight outside the Great Summer Gate.

sentences.zh: 及李苗燒絕河梁，世隆乃北遁。

translations.literal: When Li Miao burned and severed the river bridge, Shilong then fled north.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Miao burned and destroyed the river bridge, Shilong fled north.

sentences.zh: 攻建州克之，盡殺人以肆其忿。

translations.literal: He attacked Jian province and captured it, killing all to vent his rage.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked and captured Jian province, slaughtering the population to vent his fury.

sentences.zh: 至長子，與度律等共推長廣王曄為主。

translations.literal: Reaching Changzi, he together with Dulu and others jointly set up Prince Guang of Chang as leader.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzi he joined Erzhu Dulu and the others in setting up Prince Guang of Chang as their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 曄小名盆子，聞者皆以為事類赤眉。

translations.literal: Ye's childhood name was Penzi (Basin-son); those who heard of it all thought the affair resembled the Red Eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's childhood name was Penzi—Basin-son—and everyone who heard it thought the episode recalled the Red Eyebrows rebellion.

sentences.zh: 曄以世隆為尚書令，封樂平郡王，加太傅，行司州牧，會兆于河陽。

translations.literal: Ye appointed Shilong Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Leping commandery, added Grand Tutor, and acting Governor of Si province; he joined Zhao at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye made Shilong Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Leping commandery, appointed him Grand Tutor and acting Governor of Si province, and joined Erzhu Zhao at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 兆既平京邑，讓世隆曰：「叔父在朝多時，耳目應廣，如何令天柱受禍？

translations.literal: Once Zhao had pacified the capital region, he reproached Shilong: "Uncle, you were long at court and should have had wide access to information—how could you let the Heavenly Pillar suffer calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Once Erzhu Zhao had pacified the capital, he upbraided Shilong: "Uncle, you spent years at court with eyes and ears everywhere—how could you let the Heavenly Pillar come to harm?

sentences.zh: 」按劍嗔目，詞色甚厲。

translations.literal: He grasped his sword, glared in fury, his words and expression extremely stern.
translations.idiomatic: Hand on his sword, eyes blazing, he spoke in a voice of fury.

sentences.zh: 世隆遜辭拜謝，然後得已，而深恨之。

translations.literal: Shilong offered humble apologies and bowed in submission, and only then was he spared, but he deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong bowed and pleaded for mercy until Zhao relented, but he never forgave the humiliation.

sentences.zh: 時仲遠亦自滑台入京。

translations.literal: At this time Zhongyuan also entered the capital from Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Erzhu Zhongyuan also entered the capital from Huatai.

sentences.zh: 世隆與兄弟密謀，慮元曄母幹豫朝政，伺其母衛氏出行，遣數十騎如劫賊，於京巷殺之。

translations.literal: Shilong and his brothers plotted in secret, fearing that Ye's mother Yuan would meddle in court affairs; when her mother Lady Wei went out, they sent several dozen horsemen like bandits and killed her in a capital lane.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and his brothers plotted in secret, fearing that Ye's mother would meddle in affairs of state. When Lady Wei, Ye's mother, went out, they sent several dozen horsemen disguised as bandits to kill her in a capital street.

sentences.zh: 公私驚愕，莫識所由。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners alike were shocked; no one knew who was responsible.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were stunned; no one knew who had done it.

sentences.zh: 尋縣榜，以千萬錢募賊。

translations.literal: Soon a public notice was posted, offering ten million cash to reward capture of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a public notice was posted offering ten million cash for the capture of the killers.

sentences.zh: 百姓知之，莫不喪氣。

translations.literal: When the common people learned of it, none failed to lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the people realized what had happened, their spirits sank.

sentences.zh: 尋又以曄疏遠，欲推立節閔帝。

translations.literal: Soon, finding Ye too distant and isolated, they sought to set up the Jiemin Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Ye too remote and powerless, they soon moved to install the Jiemin Emperor instead.

sentences.zh: 而度律意在南陽王，乃曰：「廣陵不言，何以主天下？

translations.literal: But Dulu favored the Prince of Nanyang and said, "If Guangling does not speak, how can he rule the realm?
translations.idiomatic: But Erzhu Dulu favored the Prince of Nanyang and objected: "Guangling cannot speak—how can he rule the realm?

sentences.zh: 」後知能語，遂行廢立。

translations.literal: Later learning that he could speak, they then carried out the deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned that Guangling could in fact speak, they proceeded with the deposition and enthronement.

sentences.zh: 初，世隆之為僕射，尚書文簿，在家省閱。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shilong served as Vice Director, he reviewed Secretariat documents at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilong first served as Vice Director, he reviewed Secretariat documents at home.

sentences.zh: 性聰解，又畏榮，深自克勉，留心几案，傍接賓客，遂有解了之名。

translations.literal: Clever by nature and also in awe of Rong, he restrained himself deeply, tended diligently to his desk work, and received guests at his side, and thus gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted by nature and still in awe of Erzhu Rong, he applied himself rigorously to his paperwork, received guests attentively, and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 榮死之後，無所顧憚。

translations.literal: After Rong's death, there was nothing left to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, nothing held him back.

sentences.zh: 及為令，常使尚書郎宋游道、邢昕在其宅聽事，東西別座，受納訴訟，稱命施行。

translations.literal: Once he became Director, he routinely had Secretariat Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin hear cases at his residence, seated separately east and west, receiving and adjudicating lawsuits, and issuing orders in his name.
translations.idiomatic: As Director he routinely had Secretariat Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin hear cases at his residence, seated in separate wings east and west, taking petitions and issuing orders in his own name.

sentences.zh: 既總朝政，生殺自由，公行淫泆，信任群小，隨情與奪。

translations.literal: Having seized overall control of court affairs, he held life and death at his whim, openly indulged in licentiousness, trusted petty men, and granted or seized at will.
translations.idiomatic: With full control of the government, he held the power of life and death, indulged his appetites openly, trusted sycophants, and dispensed favor or punishment as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 又兄弟群從，各擁強兵，割剝四海，極其貪虐。

translations.literal: Moreover, his brothers and kinsmen each commanded strong forces, exploiting the realm to the utmost in greed and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers and cousins each commanded powerful armies, plundering the realm with unrestrained greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 奸諂蛆酷，多見信用；

translations.literal: Flatterers and venomous sycophants were widely trusted;
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers and vicious toadies won his trust;

sentences.zh: 溫良名士，罕豫腹心。

translations.literal: while mild and upright gentlemen were rarely admitted to his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: gentle, upright men were rarely admitted to his confidence.

sentences.zh: 於是天下之人，莫不厭毒。

translations.literal: Thereupon none under Heaven failed to loathe and detest them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the whole realm loathed them.

sentences.zh: 世隆尋讓太傅。

translations.literal: Shilong soon relinquished the Grand Tutor title.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong soon resigned the Grand Tutorship.

sentences.zh: 節閔特置儀同三師之官，位次上公之下，以世隆為之。

translations.literal: The Jiemin Emperor specially established the office of Honored Equal to the Three Preceptors, ranked below the senior dukes; Shilong was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiemin Emperor created a new office, Honored Equal to the Three Preceptors, ranked just below the senior dukes, and appointed Shilong to it.

sentences.zh: 贈其父買珍相國、錄尚書事、大司馬。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father Maizhen as Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat Affairs, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his father Maizhen as Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武起義兵，仲遠、度律等愚贛恃強，不以為慮，而世隆獨深憂恐。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised his banner of righteous troops, Zhongyuan, Dulu, and the others, stupid and obstinate in relying on their strength, gave it no thought, but Shilong alone was deeply fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised his army in righteous revolt, Erzhu Zhongyuan, Erzhu Dulu, and the others—blind to the danger in their own strength—paid it no heed, but Shilong alone was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及天光等敗于韓陵，世隆請赦天下，節閔不許。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Shilong requested a general amnesty; the Jiemin Emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Shilong pleaded for a general amnesty; the Jiemin Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿既據河橋，盡殺世隆黨附，令行台長孫承業詣闕奏狀，掩執世隆及兄彥伯，俱斬之。

translations.literal: Once Husi Chun had seized River Bridge, he killed all of Shilong's adherents, sent the Branch Commandery Chief Changsun Chengye to the palace to report the facts, and seized Shilong and his elder brother Yanbo, executing them both.
translations.idiomatic: Once Husi Chun held River Bridge, he slaughtered Shilong's followers, sent Branch Commandery Chief Changsun Chengye to the palace with a report, and seized Shilong and his elder brother Erzhu Yanbo. Both were executed.

sentences.zh: 初，世隆曾與吏部尚書元世俊握槊，忽聞局上詨然有聲，一局子盡倒立，世隆甚惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shilong had played pitch-pot with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun when suddenly a loud crack was heard on the board and every piece stood upright at once; Shilong found this very ominous.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Shilong was playing pitch-pot with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun when a loud crack sounded on the board and every piece flipped upright at once. Shilong took it as a terrible omen.

sentences.zh: 又曾晝寢，其妻奚氏忽見一人持世隆首去。

translations.literal: On another occasion while napping by day, his wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying off Shilong's head.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while he napped by day, his wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying off Shilong's head.

sentences.zh: 奚氏驚，就視，而世隆寢如故。

translations.literal: Lady Xi was alarmed and went to look; Shilong was still sleeping as before.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, she went to look—Shilong was still sleeping peacefully.

sentences.zh: 既覺，謂妻曰：「向夢人斷我頭持去，意殊不適。

translations.literal: When he awoke he told his wife, "Just now I dreamed that someone cut off my head and carried it away—I feel quite unwell.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he told her, "I dreamed someone cut off my head and carried it away. I feel ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 」又此年正月晦日，令、僕並不上省，西門不開。

translations.literal: On the last day of the first month that year, neither the Director nor the Vice Directors attended the Secretariat, and the western gate was not opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the first month that year, neither the Director nor the Vice Directors came to the Secretariat, and the western gate remained closed.

sentences.zh: 忽有河內太守田帖家奴，告省門亭長云：「今旦為令王借車牛一乘，終日于洛濱遊觀。

translations.literal: Suddenly a slave of Tian Tie, Administrator of Henei commandery, reported to the gate watch-captain of the Secretariat: "This morning I borrowed a cart and ox for the Director-lord Wang, and spent the whole day touring along the Luo riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Then a slave belonging to Tian Tie, Administrator of Henei commandery, reported to the Secretariat gate watch-captain: "This morning I borrowed a cart and ox for Director Wang and spent the entire day sightseeing along the Luo riverbank.

sentences.zh: 至晚，王還省，將車出東掖門，始覺車上無褥，請為記識。

translations.literal: In the evening the Director returned to the Secretariat and was about to drive out the Eastern Side Gate when he noticed there was no cushion in the cart and asked that this be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening Director Wang returned to the Secretariat and was about to drive out the Eastern Side Gate when he noticed the cart had no cushion and asked that this be noted.

sentences.zh: 」亭長以令僕不上，西門不開，無跡入者。

translations.literal: The watch-captain replied that neither Director nor Vice Directors had come to office and the western gate had not been opened—there was no sign anyone had entered.
translations.idiomatic: The watch-captain replied that neither the Director nor the Vice Directors had come to office, the western gate had not been opened, and no one could have entered.

sentences.zh: 此奴固陳不已，公文列訴。

translations.literal: The slave persisted without cease and filed an official complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The slave would not drop the matter and filed a formal complaint.

sentences.zh: 尚書都令史謝遠疑，謂妄有假借，白世隆，付曹推驗。

translations.literal: Secretariat Chief Clerk Xie Yuan found it suspicious, thinking it a false claim, reported to Shilong, and the matter was referred to the bureau for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Chief Clerk Xie Yuan found the story suspicious and suspected a false claim. He reported to Shilong and the case was referred for investigation.

sentences.zh: 時都官郎中穆子容究之。

translations.literal: At the time Director of Punishments Mu Zirong investigated it.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Punishments Mu Zirong was assigned to investigate.

sentences.zh: 奴言，初來時，至司空府西，欲向省。

translations.literal: The slave said that when he first arrived, he reached the west of the Minister of Works' office and intended to go to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The slave testified that when he first arrived he reached the area west of the Minister of Works' office and was heading for the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 令王嫌遲，遣催車。

translations.literal: The Director-lord, finding the delay annoying, sent someone to hurry the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang, impatient at the delay, sent someone to hurry the cart along.

sentences.zh: 車入，到省西門，王嫌牛小，系于關下槐樹，更將一青牛駕車。

translations.literal: The cart entered and reached the Secretariat's western gate; the Director-lord thought the ox too small, tied it under the catalpa tree at the checkpoint, and substituted a black ox to drive the cart.
translations.idiomatic: The cart entered and reached the Secretariat's western gate. Director Wang thought the ox too small, tied it under the catalpa tree at the gate, and swapped in a black ox.

sentences.zh: 令王著白紗、高頂帽，短小、黑色，儐從皆裙襦袴褶，握板，不似常時服章。

translations.literal: The Director-lord wore white gauze and a high-topped cap; he was short and dark; his attendants all wore skirted jackets and trouser-folds, holding tablets—not like their usual court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang wore white gauze and a high-topped cap. He was short and dark-complexioned. His attendants wore skirted jackets and riding trousers, clutching tablets—nothing like their usual court dress.

sentences.zh: 遂遣一吏將奴送入省中査事東閣內，東廂第一屋中。

translations.literal: He then sent a clerk to escort the slave into the Secretariat's Eastern Investigation Pavilion, to the first room of the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a clerk to escort the slave into the Eastern Investigation Pavilion within the Secretariat, to the first room of the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 其屋先常閉。

translations.literal: That room had long been kept closed.
translations.idiomatic: That room had long been kept locked.

sentences.zh: 奴雲，入此屋中有板床，床上無席，大有塵土，兼有甕米。

translations.literal: The slave said that inside this room there was a plank bed with no mat, much dust, and also a jar of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The slave said the room contained a plank bed with no mat, thick dust everywhere, and a jar of rice.

sentences.zh: 奴拂床坐，兼畫地戲，甕中米亦握看之。

translations.literal: The slave brushed the bed and sat down, also scrawling on the ground for amusement, and even took the rice from the jar to examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The slave brushed off the bed and sat down, scratched figures on the ground for amusement, and even scooped rice from the jar to examine it.

sentences.zh: 子容與謝遠看之，閉極久，全無開跡。

translations.literal: Zirong and Xie Yuan inspected it; it had been closed for a very long time with no sign of having been opened.
translations.idiomatic: Zirong and Xie Yuan inspected the room. It had been sealed for a long time and showed no sign of entry.

sentences.zh: 及入，狀皆符同。

translations.literal: But once they entered, everything matched the account.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they opened it, every detail matched the slave's testimony.

sentences.zh: 具以此對世隆。

translations.literal: They reported all this to Shilong in full.
translations.idiomatic: They reported the full findings to Shilong.

sentences.zh: 世隆悵然，意以為惡。

translations.literal: Shilong was deeply dismayed and took it as an evil omen.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was stricken and took it as a portent of doom.

sentences.zh: 未幾見誅。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed.

sentences.zh: 世隆弟世承，莊帝時位侍中，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: Shilong's younger brother Shicheng, during Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's younger brother Shicheng served under Emperor Xiaozhuang as Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 人才猥劣，備員而已。

translations.literal: His talent was coarse and inferior; he was a mere placeholder.
translations.idiomatic: His abilities were crude and negligible; he was a mere figurehead.

sentences.zh: 及元顥內逼，世承守轘轅，為顥所禽。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Shicheng defended Huanyuan and was captured by Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward on the capital, Shicheng held Huanyuan Pass and was captured.

sentences.zh: 顥讓而臠之。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao reproached him and had him cut to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao denounced him and had him cut to pieces.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，贈司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Shicheng was posthumously honored as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Shicheng was posthumously honored as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 世承弟弼，字輔伯，節閔帝時，封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Shicheng's younger brother Bi, style name Fubo, during the Jiemin Emperor's reign was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng's younger brother Bi, style name Fubo, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian commandery under the Jiemin Emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Inspector of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Inspector of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之敗，欲奔梁，數日，與左右割臂為約。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Hanling, wishing to flee to Liang, after several days he and his followers cut their arms to seal a pact.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Hanling, planning to flee to Liang, he and his followers cut their arms to seal a blood oath several days later.

sentences.zh: 弼帳下都督馮紹隆為弼信待，乃說弼曰：「今方同契闊，宜當心瀝血，示眾以信。

translations.literal: Feng Shaolong, a commander on Bi's staff who was trusted by him, then said to Bi: "Now that we share this life-or-death bond, you ought to pour out your heart's blood to show the masses your sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shaolong, a commander on Bi's staff whom he trusted, urged him: "We are bound in life and death together. You should open your chest and pour out your heart's blood to prove your sincerity to the men.

sentences.zh: 」弼從之。

translations.literal: Bi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi agreed.

sentences.zh: 大集部下，弼乃踞胡床，令紹隆持刀披心。

translations.literal: He gathered his subordinates in great number; Bi then sat astride a camp chair and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled his officers. Bi seated himself on a camp chair and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest.

sentences.zh: 紹隆因推刃殺之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Shaolong thereupon drove the blade in and killed him, sending his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolong drove the blade home and killed him, then sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尒硃度律

translations.literal: Erzhu Dulu
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulu

sentences.zh: 度律，榮從父弟也，鄙樸少言。

translations.literal: Dulu was Rong's paternal cousin; uncouth and plain, he spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulu was Erzhu Rong's paternal cousin—crude, plain-spoken, and taciturn.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，封樂鄉縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lexiang county.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lexiang county.

sentences.zh: 榮死，與世隆赴晉陽。

translations.literal: When Rong died, he went with Shilong to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was killed, Erzhu Dulu went with Erzhu Shilong to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元曄之立，以度律為太尉公、四面大都督，封常山王。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established, Dulu was made Duke of Grand Commandant and Grand Commander of the Four Fronts, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Erzhu Dulu was appointed Grand Commandant Duke and Grand Commander of the Four Fronts, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 與尒硃兆入洛。

translations.literal: He entered Luoyang together with Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang together with Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兆遷晉陽，留度律鎮京師。

translations.literal: Zhao moved to Jinyang, leaving Dulu to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao moved to Jinyang and left Erzhu Dulu to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝時，為使持節、侍中、大將軍、太尉公，兼尚書令、東北道行台，與仲遠出拒義旗。

translations.literal: Under the Jiemin Emperor, he served as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, Duke of Grand Commandant, and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Secretariat of the Northeastern Route, going out with Zhongyuan to resist the banner of righteous revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiemin Emperor he held the titles Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, and Grand Commandant Duke, and concurrently served as Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Northeastern Route Mobile Secretariat, marching out with Erzhu Zhongyuan to resist Gao Huan's army of righteous revolt.

sentences.zh: 齊神武間之，與尒硃兆遂相疑貳，自敗而還。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sowed discord between them, and Zhao and he came to mutual suspicion and divided allegiance, returning after defeating themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sowed discord among them, and Erzhu Dulu and Erzhu Zhao grew mutually suspicious and disloyal, defeating themselves and retreating.

sentences.zh: 度律雖在軍戎，聚斂無厭，所經為百姓患毒。

translations.literal: Although Dulu was in the army, he plundered without limit, and wherever he passed he was a bane and poison to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Although Erzhu Dulu was on campaign, he extorted without restraint, and wherever he passed he brought misery to the common people.

sentences.zh: 其母山氏聞度律敗，遂恚憤發病。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Shan, hearing that Dulu had been defeated, grew bitter and indignant and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Shan, upon hearing of Erzhu Dulu's defeat, was overcome with anger and resentment and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 及至，母責之曰：「汝荷國恩，無狀而反，我何忍見他屠戮汝也！

translations.literal: When he arrived, his mother rebuked him, saying: "You owe the state's grace; you rebelled without cause—how can I bear to see others butcher you!
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, his mother rebuked him: "You owe the state a debt of gratitude, yet you rebelled without cause—how could I bear to watch others slaughter you!

sentences.zh: 」言終而卒，時人怪異之。

translations.literal: " Having finished speaking, she died; people of the time regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: " With those words she died, and people of the time marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 後韓陵之敗，斛斯椿先據河橋，遂西走氵壘波津，為人執送。

translations.literal: Later, after the defeat at Hanling, Husi Chun first seized the River Bridge; Dulu then fled west to Loubo Ford and was captured and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Hanling, Husi Chun seized the River Bridge first, and Erzhu Dulu fled west toward Loubo Ford, where he was captured and sent off under guard.

sentences.zh: 椿囚之，送齊神武，斬之都市。

translations.literal: Chun imprisoned him, sent him to Gao Huan, and had him executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun imprisoned him and sent him to Gao Huan, who had him executed in the public marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尒硃天光

translations.literal: Erzhu Tianguang
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang

sentences.zh: 天光，榮從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Tianguang was the grandson of Rong's grand-uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang was the grandson of Erzhu Rong's grand-uncle.

sentences.zh: 少勇決，榮特親愛之，常預軍戎謀。

translations.literal: Young, brave, and resolute, Rong was especially fond of him and often included him in military counsel.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bold and decisive; Erzhu Rong was especially fond of him and regularly included him in military planning.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，榮據並、肆，仍以天光為都將，總統肆州兵馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, Rong held Bing and Si, and again made Tianguang a frontier commander-in-chief, putting him in overall charge of Si Prefecture's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of the Xiaochang reign, when Erzhu Rong held Bing and Si, he again made Erzhu Tianguang a frontier commander-in-chief and put him in overall charge of the troops and horses of Si Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，榮向京師，委以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Rong headed for the capital and entrusted him with subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Erzhu Rong marched toward the capital and entrusted Erzhu Tianguang with affairs at home.

sentences.zh: 建義初，為肆州刺史，封長安縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he was made Inspector of Si Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Inspector of Si Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an county.

sentences.zh: 榮將討葛榮，留天光在州，鎮其根本。

translations.literal: Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong and left Tianguang in the province to secure his base.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong set out to campaign against Ge Rong, he left Erzhu Tianguang in the province to hold his rear base secure.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「我身不得至處，非汝無以稱我心。

translations.literal: He said to him: "Where I cannot go in person, without you there is no one to fulfill my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong told him, "Where I cannot go in person, no one but you can do what I wish.

sentences.zh: 」永安中，與元天穆東破邢杲。

translations.literal: " In Yong'an, together with Yuan Tianmu he defeated Xing Gao in the east.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Yong'an era he joined Yuan Tianmu in defeating Xing Gao in the east.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，天光與天穆會榮於河內。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tianguang and Tianmu joined Rong at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Erzhu Tianguang and Yuan Tianmu joined Erzhu Rong at Henei.

sentences.zh: 榮發後，並、肆不安，詔天光兼尚書僕射，為並、肆等九州行台，仍行并州事。

translations.literal: After Rong set out, Bing and Si were unsettled; an edict made Tianguang Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Secretariat over nine prefectures including Bing and Si, while he continued to administer Bingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong marched out, Bing and Si fell into unrest, and an edict appointed Erzhu Tianguang Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Mobile Secretariat for Bing, Si, and seven other prefectures, while he continued to administer Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天光至并州，部分約勒，所在寧輯。

translations.literal: When Tianguang reached Bingzhou, he apportioned and restrained troops, and wherever he was, there was peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang reached Bingzhou, he organized and disciplined the troops, and the region settled into calm.

sentences.zh: 顥破，還京師，改封廣宗郡公。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, he returned to the capital and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guangzong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao was defeated he returned to the capital and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guangzong commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，高平鎮城人赫貴連恩等為逆，共推敕勤酋長胡琛為主，號高平王。

translations.literal: Initially, He Guiyan of Gaoping garrison town and others rebelled, jointly setting up the Chie prefectural chief Hu Chen as leader and proclaiming him King of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: At first He Guiyan of Gaoping garrison town and others rose in rebellion, jointly proclaiming the Chie chieftain Hu Chen their leader with the title King of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遙臣沃野鎮賊帥破六韓忉夤。

translations.literal: He submitted from afar to Poliuhan Huyin, the bandit leader of Woye garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered distant allegiance to Poliuhan Huyin, the rebel leader of Woye garrison.

sentences.zh: 琛入據高平城，遣其大將万俟醜奴來寇涇州。

translations.literal: Chen entered and seized Gaoping city, sending his great general Moqi Chounu to raid Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chen entered and seized Gaoping city, then sent his great general Moqi Chounu to raid Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琛後與莫折念生交通，侮僈忉夤。

translations.literal: Later Chen communicated with Moqi Niansheng and insulted and despised Huyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hu Chen entered into dealings with Moqi Niansheng and treated Poliuhan Huyin with contempt.

sentences.zh: 遣使人費律如至高平，誘斬琛，為醜奴所並，與蕭寶夤相拒于安定。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy, Fei Lu, to Gaoping to lure and behead Chen; Chounu absorbed his force and confronted Xiao Baoyin at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Poliuhan Huyin sent an envoy, Fei Lu, to Gaoping to lure and kill Hu Chen; Moqi Chounu absorbed his forces and confronted Xiao Baoyin at Anding.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗還。

translations.literal: Baoyin was defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin was defeated and retreated.

sentences.zh: 建義元年夏，醜奴擊寶夤於靈州，禽之，遂僭大號。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Jianyi, Chounu attacked Baoyin at Ling Prefecture, captured him, and then arrogated a great title.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Jianyi, Moqi Chounu attacked Xiao Baoyin at Ling Prefecture, captured him, and then arrogated an imperial title.

sentences.zh: 時獲西北貢師子，因稱神獸元年，置百官。

translations.literal: At the time a tribute lion was obtained from the northwest, and accordingly he called his reign the Divine Beast era and established the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute lion had just arrived from the northwest, and on that pretext he proclaimed the Divine Beast era and established a full court bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂之，乃除天光使持節、都督、雍州刺史，率大都督武衛將軍賀拔岳、大都督侯莫陳悅等討醜奴。

translations.literal: The court was alarmed and appointed Tianguang Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner, and Inspector of Yongzhou, leading the Grand Commanders Martial Guard General Heba Yue, Grand Commander Houmochen Yue, and others to campaign against Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the court appointed Erzhu Tianguang Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner, and Inspector of Yongzhou, and ordered him to lead the Grand Commanders Martial Guard General Heba Yue, Grand Commander Houmochen Yue, and others against Moqi Chounu.

sentences.zh: 天光初行，唯有軍士千人。

translations.literal: When Tianguang first set out, he had only a thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang first set out, he had only a thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時東雍赤水蜀賊斷路，天光入關擊破之，簡取壯健。

translations.literal: At the time bandits of Chishui in Eastern Yong blocked the road; Tianguang entered the passes, defeated them, and selected the sturdy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shu bandits at Chishui in Eastern Yong blocked the road; Erzhu Tianguang entered the passes, defeated them, and drafted the able-bodied among them.

sentences.zh: 至雍，又稅人馬，合得萬疋。

translations.literal: Reaching Yong, he also levied men and horses, totaling ten thousand mounts.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong he levied men and horses as well, raising a combined force of ten thousand mounts.

sentences.zh: 以軍人寡少，停留未進。

translations.literal: Because his troops were few, he halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Because his force was still too small, he halted and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 榮遣責之，杖天光百下。

translations.literal: Rong sent someone to rebuke him and had Tianguang beaten a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong sent envoys to rebuke him and had Erzhu Tianguang beaten a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 榮復遣軍士二千人赴天光。

translations.literal: Rong again sent two thousand soldiers to join Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong then sent another two thousand soldiers to reinforce Erzhu Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光令賀拔嶽率千騎先驅，至岐州，禽其行台尉遲菩薩。

translations.literal: Tianguang ordered Heba Yue to lead a thousand horsemen as vanguard; reaching Qizhou, he captured their Mobile Secretariat chief Yuchi Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang ordered Heba Yue to lead a thousand horsemen as vanguard; at Qizhou he captured the rebel Mobile Secretariat chief Yuchi Pusa.

sentences.zh: 醜奴棄岐州走還安定。

translations.literal: Chounu abandoned Qizhou and fled back to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Chounu abandoned Qizhou and fled back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 天光發雍至岐，與嶽合勢，破醜奴，獲蕭寶夤。

translations.literal: Tianguang set out from Yong to Qi, joined forces with Yue, defeated Chounu, and captured Xiao Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang marched from Yong to Qi, joined forces with Heba Yue, defeated Moqi Chounu, and captured Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 於是涇、豳、二夏，北至靈州，及賊黨結聚之類，並降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing, Bin, the two Xias, north to Ling Prefecture, and all types of bandit gatherings submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jing, Bin, the two Xia prefectures, and the region north to Ling Prefecture, together with every cluster of rebel bands, submitted.

sentences.zh: 唯賊行台万俟道洛不下，率眾西依牽屯山，據險自守。

translations.literal: Only the bandit Mobile Secretariat chief Moqi Daoluo did not submit, leading masses west to rely on Qiantun Mountain and holding the passes in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Only the rebel Mobile Secretariat chief Moqi Daoluo refused to submit; he led his followers west to Qiantun Mountain and held the passes in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 榮責天光不獲道洛，復遣使杖之百，詔削爵為侯。

translations.literal: Rong rebuked Tianguang for not capturing Daoluo, again sent an envoy to beat him a hundred strokes, and by edict stripped his rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong rebuked Erzhu Tianguang for failing to capture Moqi Daoluo, again sent envoys to beat him a hundred strokes, and by edict reduced his rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 天光與嶽、悅等復向牽屯討之，道洛戰敗，投略陽賊帥王慶雲。

translations.literal: Tianguang with Yue, Yue, and others again marched on Qiantun to campaign against him; Daoluo was defeated in battle and fled to the bandit leader Wang Qingyun of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang marched on Qiantun again with Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others; Moqi Daoluo was defeated and fled to the rebel leader Wang Qingyun of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 慶雲以道洛驍果絕倫，得之甚喜，便謂大事可圖，乃自稱皇帝，以道洛為大將軍。

translations.literal: Qingyun, because Daoluo's martial prowess was unmatched, was greatly pleased to obtain him and said the great enterprise could be accomplished; he then styled himself emperor and made Daoluo Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qingyun, finding Moqi Daoluo's martial prowess unmatched, was overjoyed to have him and declared that the great enterprise could now be achieved; he styled himself emperor and made Daoluo Grand General.

sentences.zh: 天光乃入隴，至慶雲所居永洛城，破其東城。

translations.literal: Tianguang then entered Long, reaching Yongluo city where Qingyun resided, and broke its eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang then entered Long and reached Yongluo city, where Wang Qingyun was encamped, and broke through its eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 賊遂並趣西城。

translations.literal: The bandits then all rushed toward the western wall.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then all crowded into the western city.

sentences.zh: 城中無水，眾聚熱渴。

translations.literal: There was no water in the city; the masses gathered, hot and parched.
translations.idiomatic: There was no water in the city, and the trapped masses sweltered in thirst.

sentences.zh: 有人走降，言慶雲、道洛欲突出。

translations.literal: Someone fled and submitted, saying Qingyun and Daoluo intended to break out.
translations.idiomatic: A deserter came over and reported that Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daoluo planned to break out.

sentences.zh: 天光恐失賊帥，乃遣謂慶雲，可以早降，若水決，當聽諸人今夜共議。

translations.literal: Tianguang feared losing the bandit chiefs and sent word to Qingyun that he could submit early; if the water were released, he would allow everyone to deliberate together tonight.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the rebel chiefs would escape, Erzhu Tianguang sent word to Wang Qingyun that he could surrender at once; if he chose to unleash the water instead, he would still allow the rebels to discuss surrender together that night.

sentences.zh: 又謂曰：「相知須水，今為小退。

translations.literal: He also said: "Knowing you need water, we shall withdraw a little now.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Knowing you need water, we shall pull back a little for now.

sentences.zh: 」賊眾安悅，無復走心。

translations.literal: " The bandit masses were reassured and lost the will to flee.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebel masses were reassured and no longer thought of fleeing.

sentences.zh: 天光密使軍人多作木槍，各長七尺，至昏，布立人馬，為防衛之勢，又伏人槍中。

translations.literal: Tianguang secretly had the soldiers make many wooden pikes, each seven feet long; at dusk he deployed men and horses in a defensive posture, and also hid men among the pikes.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang secretly ordered his soldiers to make many wooden stakes, each seven feet long; at dusk he deployed men and horses in a defensive array and hid troops among the stakes.

sentences.zh: 其夜，慶雲、道洛果突出，至槍，馬各傷倒。

translations.literal: That night Qingyun and Daoluo did break out; reaching the pikes, the horses were each wounded and fell.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daoluo did break out; when they reached the stakes, horse after horse was wounded and brought down.

sentences.zh: 伏兵便起，同時禽獲。

translations.literal: The hidden troops rose at once and captured them simultaneously.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden troops sprang up and captured them all at once.

sentences.zh: 賊窮，乞降而已。

translations.literal: The bandits were desperate and could only beg to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, driven to desperation, could only beg to surrender.

sentences.zh: 天光、嶽、悅等議悉阬之，死者萬七千人，分其家口。

translations.literal: Tianguang, Yue, Yue, and others deliberated to bury them all alive; seventeen thousand died, and their household members were distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang, Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others decided to massacre them all; seventeen thousand were killed, and their families were distributed as booty.

sentences.zh: 於是三秦、河、渭、瓜、梁、鄯善咸來款順。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Three Qins, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Three Qins, the He and Wei river basins, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came forward to submit.

sentences.zh: 詔復天光前官爵。

translations.literal: An edict restored Tianguang's former titles and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Erzhu Tianguang's former titles and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 岳聞榮死，還涇州以待，天光亦下隴，與嶽圖入洛之策。

translations.literal: Yue heard Rong was dead, returned to Jing Prefecture to wait; Tianguang also descended from Long and with Yue plotted a plan to enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue heard that Erzhu Rong was dead, he returned to Jing Prefecture to wait; Erzhu Tianguang also came down from Long and joined Heba Yue in plotting a march on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既而莊帝進天光爵為廣宗王，元曄又以為隴西王。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Xiaozhuang advanced Tianguang's rank to Prince of Guangzong; Yuan Ye again made him Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Xiaozhuang advanced Erzhu Tianguang to Prince of Guangzong, and Yuan Ye in turn invested him as Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 及聞尒硃兆已入京，天光乃輕騎向都，見世隆等，尋便還雍。

translations.literal: When he heard Erzhu Zhao had already entered the capital, Tianguang made a light cavalry ride to the capital, saw Shilong and the others, and soon returned to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Erzhu Zhao had already entered the capital, Erzhu Tianguang rode lightly to the capital, met with Erzhu Shilong and the others, and soon returned to Yong.

sentences.zh: 世隆等議廢元曄，更舉親賢，遣告天光。

translations.literal: Shilong and the others deliberated deposing Yuan Ye and raising a close and worthy man, and sent word to Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and his faction deliberated deposing Yuan Ye and enthroning a close and worthy kinsman, and sent word to Erzhu Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光與定策，立節閔帝。

translations.literal: Tianguang joined in fixing the plan and enthroned the Jiemin Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang joined in settling the plan and helped enthrone the Jiemin Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又加開府儀同三司、尚書令、關西大行台。

translations.literal: He was further given Opener of an Office with Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Mobile Secretariat of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted Opener of an Office with Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Mobile Secretariat of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 天光北出夏州，遣將討宿勤明達，禽之，送洛。

translations.literal: Tianguang marched north out of Xia Prefecture, sent a general to campaign against Suqin Mingda, captured him, and sent him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang marched north out of Xia Prefecture, sent a general against Suqin Mingda, captured him, and sent him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時費也頭帥紇豆陵伊利、万俟受洛於等據有河西，未有所附。

translations.literal: At the time the Feiyeotou chiefs Heldouling Yili and Moqi Shouluoyu and others held Hexi and had not yet attached themselves to any side.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Feiyeotou chiefs Heldouling Yili and Moqi Shouluoyu and others held Hexi and had not yet pledged themselves to any faction.

sentences.zh: 天光以齊神武起兵信都，內懷憂恐，不暇他事。

translations.literal: Because Gao Huan had raised troops at Xindu, Tianguang harbored worry and fear within and had no leisure for other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gao Huan had raised troops at Xindu, Erzhu Tianguang was inwardly anxious and had no leisure for other matters.

sentences.zh: 伊利等，但微遣備之而已。

translations.literal: As for Yili and the others, he only sent light precautions against them.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yili and the others, he sent only light detachments to watch them.

sentences.zh: 又除大司馬。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 時神武軍既振，尒硃兆、仲遠等並經敗退。

translations.literal: By then Gao Huan's army had gained momentum, and Zhao and Zhongyuan had already been defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gao Huan's army had gained momentum, and Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Zhongyuan, and the others had already been defeated and driven back.

sentences.zh: 世隆累使徵天光，天光不從。

translations.literal: Shilong repeatedly sent envoys to summon Tianguang; Tianguang did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong repeatedly sent envoys to summon Erzhu Tianguang, but Tianguang refused to come.

sentences.zh: 後令斛斯椿苦要天光云：「非王無以能定，豈可坐看宗家之滅？

translations.literal: Later he had Husi Chun urgently press Tianguang, saying: "Without you, the prince, no one can settle matters—how can you sit and watch the clan's destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Later Erzhu Shilong had Husi Chun urgently press Erzhu Tianguang, saying, "Without Your Highness no one can settle matters—how can you sit by and watch the clan be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 」天光不得已，東下，與仲遠等敗于韓陵。

translations.literal: " Tianguang had no choice, marched east, and with Zhongyuan and others was defeated at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Tianguang had no choice; he marched east and, together with Erzhu Zhongyuan and the others, was defeated at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿等先還，於河橋拒之，天光不得度，西北走，被執，與度律並送于神武。

translations.literal: Husi Chun and the others returned first and blocked him at the River Bridge; Tianguang could not cross, fled northwest, was seized, and together with Dulu was sent to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun and the others returned first and blocked the River Bridge; Erzhu Tianguang could not cross, fled northwest, was captured, and was sent together with Erzhu Dulu to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武送於洛，斬於都市。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sent them to Luoyang and had them executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent them to Luoyang, where both were executed in the public marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尒硃專恣，分裂天下，各據一方，賞罰自出，而天光有定關西之功，差不酷暴，比之兆與仲遠，為不同矣。

translations.literal: The Erzhu clan was willful and autocratic, splitting the realm and each holding a region, dispensing rewards and punishments on their own; yet Tianguang had the merit of pacifying Guanxi, was somewhat less cruel and violent, and compared with Zhao and Zhongyuan, was not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Erzhu clan was willful and autocratic, splitting the realm so that each branch held its own territory and dispensed rewards and punishments at will; yet Erzhu Tianguang had the achievement of pacifying Guanxi and was somewhat less cruel and violent—compared with Erzhu Zhao and Erzhu Zhongyuan, he was a different sort of man altogether.

sentences.zh: 論曰：魏自宣武之後，政道頗虧。

translations.literal: Commentary says: From Emperor Xuanwu onward, the way of governance was greatly impaired.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: From the reign of Emperor Xuanwu onward, the way of governance was greatly impaired.

sentences.zh: 及明皇幼沖，女主南面。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming came to the throne as a minor, the empress dowager faced south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming acceded as a child, the empress dowager ruled from behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 始則於忠專恣，繼以元叉權重，居官者肆其聚斂，乘勢者極其陵暴，於是四海囂然，已有群飛之漸。

translations.literal: First Yu Zhong was willful and autocratic, then Yuan Cha held heavy power; officeholders indulged in plunder, those who seized advantage reached the extreme in bullying and violence; thus the four seas were in uproar, and there were already the first signs of mass flight.
translations.idiomatic: First Yu Zhong ruled with unchecked willfulness, then Yuan Cha amassed overwhelming power; officeholders plundered without restraint, and those who seized the moment bullied and oppressed to the utmost. The realm fell into uproar, and the first signs of mass upheaval were already visible.

sentences.zh: 逮於靈後反政，宣淫於朝，傾覆之徵，於此至矣。

translations.literal: Reaching Empress Dowager Ling's resumption of rule, she flaunted debauchery at court, and the signs of overturning reached their fullest here.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, she flaunted debauchery at court, and the signs of dynastic collapse reached their fullest point.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮緣將帥之列，藉部眾之威，屬天下暴虐，人神怨憤。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, arising from the ranks of generals and relying on the might of his troops, at a time when the realm was violently oppressive and men and spirits alike were aggrieved and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong rose from the ranks of military commanders and relied on the might of his troops at a time when the realm was violently oppressed and both men and spirits seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 遂有匡頹拯弊之志，援主逐惡之功。

translations.literal: Thereupon had the will to right the tottering and save the ruined, and the achievement of supporting the ruler and driving out evil.
translations.idiomatic: He thus conceived the will to right a tottering state and rescue a ruined order, and won the achievement of supporting the ruler and driving out evil.

sentences.zh: 及夫禽葛榮，誅元顥，戮邢杲，揃韓婁，醜奴、寶夤，咸梟馬市，然則榮之功烈，亦已茂矣。

translations.literal: When he captured Ge Rong, executed Yuan Hao, killed Xing Gao, cut down Han Lou, Chounu, and Baoyin—all displayed at the Horse Market—then Rong's feats of merit were indeed abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ge Rong, executed Yuan Hao, killed Xing Gao, cut down Han Lou, and had Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin all displayed at the Horse Market—thus Erzhu Rong's feats of merit were indeed abundant.

sentences.zh: 而始則希覬非望，睥睨宸極，終乃靈後、少帝，沈流不反。

translations.literal: Yet at first he cherished illicit ambitions and looked askance at the throne; in the end the Empress Dowager Ling and the young emperor were drowned and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at first he harbored illicit ambitions and looked askance at the imperial throne; in the end Empress Dowager Ling and the young emperor were drowned and never returned.

sentences.zh: 河陰之下，衣冠塗地，其所以得罪人神者焉。

translations.literal: At the He'yin massacre, officials and gentry were strewn across the ground—that is how he offended men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: At the He'yin massacre officials and gentry were strewn across the ground—that is how he earned the condemnation of both men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 至於末跡凶忍，地逼亦已除矣。

translations.literal: As for his final tracks, cruel and ruthless, he was eliminated when his power reached its limit.
translations.idiomatic: As for his final course, cruel and ruthless to the end, he was eliminated once his power had reached its limit.

sentences.zh: 而朝無謀難之宰，國乏折沖之將，遂使餘孽相糾，還成嚴敵。

translations.literal: Yet the court had no minister to plan for difficulty, and the state lacked generals to repel the foe; thus the remaining spawn entangled one another and again became formidable enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court had no minister capable of planning for crisis, and the state lacked generals to repel invaders; thus the surviving remnants entangled with one another and again became formidable enemies.

sentences.zh: 隆實指蹤，兆為戎首，山河失險，莊帝幽崩。

translations.literal: Shilong in fact directed strategy, Zhao was the military ringleader; passes and rivers were lost, and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in secret imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong in fact directed strategy, Erzhu Zhao was the military ringleader; strategic passes and rivers were lost, and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in secret confinement.

sentences.zh: 宗屬分方，作威跋扈，廢帝立主，回天倒日；

translations.literal: The clan kindred divided the realm, wielded power arrogantly, deposed emperors and enthroned lords, reversing heaven and overturning the sun;
translations.idiomatic: The clan kindred carved up the realm, swaggered in power, deposed emperors and enthroned new rulers, reversing heaven and overturning the sun;

sentences.zh: 揃剝黎獻，割裂神州，刑賞任心，征伐自己。

translations.literal: They stripped the people, carved up the sacred land, made punishments and rewards as their hearts pleased, and launched campaigns as they themselves willed.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped the common people, carved up the sacred land, dispensed punishments and rewards as their hearts pleased, and launched campaigns at their own whim.

sentences.zh: 天下之命，縣于數胡，喪亂弘多，遂至於此。

translations.literal: The fate of the realm hung on a few barbarians; calamity and disorder multiplied greatly, and thus it reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the realm hung on a handful of barbarian chieftains; calamity and disorder multiplied until the realm reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 豈非天將去之，始以共定；

translations.literal: Was it not that Heaven was about to remove Wei—at first using them together to stabilize;
translations.idiomatic: Was this not Heaven's way of removing Wei—at first using them together to stabilize the realm;

sentences.zh: 終於惡稔，以至殄滅。

translations.literal: And in the end, when wickedness was fully ripe, bringing them to total extinction.
translations.idiomatic: and in the end, when their wickedness had fully ripened, bringing them to total extinction?

sentences.zh: 抑亦魏紓其難，齊以驅除矣。

translations.literal: Yet Wei also eased its difficulty, and Qi drove them out and eliminated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei also eased its own crisis thereby, and Qi drove the Erzhu clan out and eliminated them.
